requirements.title: Definition and identity
requirements.observable_behavior:
A definition has exactly `schema`, `types` and `aggregate`. Its identity is `digest("aggregate-definition",definition)` under the common domain rule. Types, units, time configuration, window, mappings, observation policy and pending-exposure policy are therefore part of the identity. `evaluate` receives `{kind:"AGGREGATE",request:<input>}` through the new protocol. The complete definition bytes are present in request.definition and their digest is request.definition_digest. The request also binds the exact specification manifest. Neither a type identifier nor an aggregate name can select an external definition.

The first profile supports the five scalar type kinds IDENTITY, STRING, BOOLEAN, INTEGER and DECIMAL. A typed value is `{type_ref,value}`. Type identity is scoped by the complete definition digest plus type_ref. Type arrays are sorted by id in UTF-8 order; IDs are unique. STRING permits any scalar Unicode string, IDENTITY requires a nonempty string, BOOLEAN requires a JSON Boolean. INTEGER and DECIMAL use the common canonical exact-number grammars. A nonnegative flag on those two kinds rejects negative payloads; the flag must be false for other kinds. Unit is null except for a DECIMAL quantity, which may name a nonempty unit. Unit equality is exact and conversion is forbidden. INTEGER quantities and composite group elements are outside this scalar profile and must use a later definition rather than be coerced to strings.

requirements.title: Reducers, result types and bounds
requirements.observable_behavior:
COUNT and CARDINALITY require a nonnegative INTEGER result type without a unit. SUM requires a nonnegative DECIMAL result type with an explicit unit. SUM adds quantities of that exact type; decimal precision is mathematical, not binary floating point. COUNT's contribution for each selected operation/mapping or selected historical event is the typed result value `"1"`. CARDINALITY declares a nonnull element_type resolving to any supported scalar type; the other reducers require element_type=null. A CARDINALITY contribution is one typed element, not an integer count.

The bound is a nonnegative value of the result type. Operator is LT, LTE, GT or GTE and means the corresponding exact numerical comparison. Definition acceptance establishes its type, not that any proposal satisfies its bound. COUNT begins at zero; SUM at zero of its unit; CARDINALITY at the empty finite set and returns its size. A set accumulator contains full typed values in canonical byte order, with no duplicates. Its final count is a natural-integer string.

requirements.title: Field mappings and qualifiers
requirements.observable_behavior:
An operation has a nonempty occurrence identifier, step identifier and a sorted, unique array of named typed fields. Occurrences are unique within one input and sort by UTF-8 identifier bytes. Every field is type-checked even if no mapping selects it. Field names are local to the supplied operation, not English descriptions. A mapping contains a unique id, sorted unique nonempty step_ids, qualifier, ordered key_fields and contribution. Mappings sort by id. Its step set selects applicable operations; its qualifier then decides inclusion. Every selected pair of operation and mapping contributes exactly once. Contributions are derived by the evaluator, not supplied as a second caller-controlled projection.

A FIELD operand reads the exactly named field. A LITERAL operand carries an admitted typed value. EQUAL compares equal nominal types and exact values. MEMBER requires every member to have the operand's nominal type; the members form a canonical sorted set. COMPARE accepts equal INTEGER or DECIMAL types and the declared exact comparison. BOOLEAN is its literal truth value. ALL and ANY evaluate every operand, with empty ALL true and empty ANY false; NOT complements its operand. Qualifiers contain no unavailable value, callback or English evaluation. Missing fields, incompatible operands or unsupported expressions are input errors, including beneath a Boolean branch whose other operand already decides the result. Qualifier static structure and literals are checked at definition admission; field availability and operand compatibility are checked against each applicable operation before running its qualifier. A field needed by a false-qualified operation's key or contribution is still required and type-correct; false qualification is not a bypass around input integrity.

For each selected pair, key_fields reads a nonempty tuple whose types equal aggregate.key_types position for position. The order of tuple components matters. COUNT mappings have contribution `{kind:"COUNT"}`; SUM and CARDINALITY mappings name the contribution field and matching kind. Their values have the result or element type respectively. A mapping's contribution kind must equal the aggregate reducer. Mapping field references need not occur in operations for unlisted steps, but all supplied operation fields still have valid types.

requirements.title: Pending exposure and partitions
requirements.observable_behavior:
The definition explicitly selects INCLUDE_ALL_RESERVED or EXCLUDE_RESERVED. With EXCLUDE_RESERVED, pending must be empty; supplying it is invalid, rather than silently ignoring exposure. INCLUDE_ALL_RESERVED admits pending rows with reservation, mapping, occurrence, key and typed contribution. The mapping exists, the tuple types match, and the contribution has the same kind/type meaning as a newly derived contribution. Pending rows sort by the canonical bytes of `[reservation,mapping,occurrence,key]`; these keys are unique. A pending contribution sharing a new operation's occurrence is invalid. Pending records are host-supplied reservation assertions for this evaluator; the shared-budget transition role derives them from retained state.

PER_ACTION partitions new contributions by `(occurrence,key)` and requires EXCLUDE_RESERVED and no committed source. ROLLING and CALENDAR partition by each distinct grouping tuple in the newly derived contributions. A pending contribution contributes only to a partition with its same tuple. Pending exposure is included regardless of its reservation time; only committed history is filtered through the current window. This is an explicit reservation-counting policy, not a default interpretation of completed-effect limits.

Partition order compares the canonical bytes of `{occurrence,key}`. Occurrence is null for shared-window partitions. The empty new-contribution set produces no partitions and a SATISFIED result after structural, reference, type, binding and limit admission. No observations are requested when there are no partitions. Supplying any observation in that case is invalid. This vacuous result does not authorize an unrelated business operation.

Pending-only tuples do not create partitions and are not invalid merely because this proposal addresses another tuple. They remain retained by their owning ledger and affect a later proposal for their tuple. This preserves evaluation of the partitions affected by the proposed work; it does not clear unrelated reservations.

requirements.title: Clock and temporal configuration
requirements.observable_behavior:
Definition.time supplies clock_source and precision SECOND or NANOSECOND. The supplied clock source must match. AVAILABLE uses exactly the selected instant precision; UNAVAILABLE uses null. All AVAILABLE observation and event instants use the same precision. Calendar/date validity is checked, not just the schema pattern. No ambient clock or local timezone is consulted.

A nonempty evaluation with UNAVAILABLE clock returns INDETERMINATE partitions with null accumulators/results and sole reason TIME_UNAVAILABLE, including PER_ACTION. Before that outcome, perform all structural, reference, type and directly checkable integrity checks. Query digest and future-time checks needing the absent instant do not run. An empty, admitted proposal remains vacuously satisfied.

Before TIME_UNAVAILABLE, validate every supplied observation's shape, scalar payloads, calendar dates, precision, source identity, coverage ordering, event field/qualifier/contribution types, statistic key/type/accumulator and key inventory, and static freshness declarations. Reject malformed coverage even without a clock. Limits still apply. Skip derived query equality, future as_of, current required-interval containment/equality and freshness evaluation, because these require the absent instant. Distinct reports and conflicting event terminal states are usability findings, so TIME_UNAVAILABLE takes precedence over those conflicts when the clock is absent.

ROLLING duration_seconds is positive, exact and representable on the selected precision grid. The required interval runs from evaluation minus duration through evaluation, with the two explicit endpoint flags. CALENDAR uses its declared timezone and pinned IANA tzdb 2025a. Convert evaluation to local Gregorian date, select the beginning of its declared DAY, WEEK, MONTH, QUARTER or YEAR, then convert that boundary to UTC. WEEK uses the declared starting weekday. YEAR uses the declared fiscal starting month; QUARTER uses successive three-month periods anchored to that month. All calendar fields remain explicit even where a selected period does not use an anchor. Calendar intervals end at evaluation, not at the future period end. The start/end flags apply to this elapsed prefix.

For an ambiguous local boundary, EARLIER_OFFSET chooses the earlier UTC instant and LATER_OFFSET the later one; INVALID refuses. For a nonexistent boundary, SHIFT_FORWARD adds the offset gap to the nominal local boundary, SHIFT_BACK subtracts it, and INVALID refuses. These rules do not reinterpret an input UTC instant. Arithmetic outside years 0001–9999 or a precision-grid overflow gives LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Unsupported timezone or an INVALID boundary choice gives INPUT_INVALID. A UTC host process may implement this arithmetic but cannot choose the policy's zone.

Unused calendar anchors are admitted and remain part of definition identity but have no effect on period selection. Thus two DAY definitions with different valid fiscal anchors have different identities and the same mathematical window for identical clocks.

requirements.title: Committed source and query
requirements.observable_behavior:
ROLLING and CALENDAR require a nonnull committed_source. PER_ACTION requires null and an empty observations array. The source declares provider, source, freshness, ordered key_fields, qualifier and contribution mapping. Its qualifier has the same exact language as proposal qualifiers. Each ACTIVE event's fields must supply the required key and contribution fields and type-correct qualifier operands. Events count once per source event identity, not once per proposal mapping.

For nonempty shared-window evaluation with an available clock derive the query object with exactly `definition_digest`, `interval` and `keys`. Interval is `{start,end,start_inclusive,end_inclusive}` using the selected precision and calculated bounds. Keys is the canonical sorted unique list of proposal grouping tuples. The request digest is `digest("aggregate-query",query)`. Each observation must bind this digest and the exact declared provider and source. Observations never select a different query, unit, aggregate definition, grouping or endpoint policy.

An observation is UNAVAILABLE, INCOMPLETE, or AVAILABLE. Unavailable/incomplete records retain query identity and evidence reference without fabricated revision or time. AVAILABLE includes nonempty revision, as_of, coverage and either a complete EVENT_SNAPSHOT or a complete STATISTIC bundle. Future as_of is invalid. Coverage is a well-formed interval, start no later than end, within the representable domain. All active event instants and values are validated before window or qualifier filtering. RETRACTED terminal records contain only id and state. A retraction is an explicit provider report; there is no inferred cancellation or signed correction.

requirements.title: Observation usability
requirements.observable_behavior:
Collapse byte-identical observations first. Missing observation yields OBSERVATION_MISSING; one UNAVAILABLE yields OBSERVATION_UNAVAILABLE; one INCOMPLETE yields OBSERVATION_INCOMPLETE. More than one distinct report yields OBSERVATION_CONFLICT. This bounded interface accepts one complete returned query bundle, not independently merged partial responses. A host that has several source responses must establish one complete attributable bundle under its declared provider contract; it may not fabricate completeness. Changing evidence identifiers does not authorize choosing between competing bundles.

NONE freshness accepts any otherwise usable nonfuture record. MAX_AGE accepts when evaluation minus as_of is at most the declared exact seconds; the duration obeys the precision grid. EXACT_REVISION requires exact revision equality. Failed freshness gives OBSERVATION_STALE. Event-snapshot coverage must contain the required interval, including each required inclusive endpoint; failed coverage gives OBSERVATION_INCOMPLETE. STATISTIC coverage must equal the required interval exactly because a wider statistic cannot be trimmed without history. A wrong statistic interval is INPUT_INVALID, not a stale fact.

One event snapshot contains the terminal state for each supplied event ID at its revision. Collapse exact duplicate events; two different records for one ID yield OBSERVATION_CONFLICT without choosing ACTIVE, RETRACTED, latest time or array order. Different supplied snapshots at later revisions may legitimately revise or retract an event; the pure evaluator has no hidden memory that overrides the selected current bundle. Within one snapshot select only ACTIVE events in the required interval, satisfying the declared source qualifier and matching a proposal partition's key. Zero selected events gives the reducer identity. Complete absence is distinct from unavailable history.

Revision identifiers are opaque equality tokens. There is no lexical, numerical or temporal revision ordering, and EXACT_REVISION may name any exact selected token. A complete snapshot may omit an inactive event or include its RETRACTED terminal state; both contribute zero. Authentic completeness, disclosed corrections and nonrollback selection are host premises, not deductions from revision spelling. Event order is immaterial after exact duplicate collapse. Statistics sort by canonical key bytes and have unique keys. Types, mappings, step identifier lists, operation rows, named fields, predicate MEMBER sets and pending rows must arrive in their specified sorted order; violations are admission errors. Observation arrays and snapshot event arrays may arrive in any order, subject to their defined duplicate/conflict handling.

A statistic bundle contains exactly one entry for every query key and no extra or duplicate key. COUNT requires a natural integer SCALAR; SUM a canonical nonnegative SCALAR of the definition's fixed unit; CARDINALITY a SET of the exact element type. No field may present a CARDINALITY count as a substitute for its set. A statistic asserts the accumulator for the exact bound query; provider truth and its event provenance are host responsibilities. Scalar statistics are supported by this evaluator but insufficient for identifying settled reservations; the initial shared-budget ledger therefore requires event history.

requirements.title: Results and precedence
requirements.observable_behavior:
After a usable committed accumulator, add the partition's included pending contributions and all new contributions exactly once. SUM uses exact addition, COUNT adds one per contribution, CARDINALITY unions typed elements. Compare the resulting scalar or set size with the bound. A violated partition has reason BOUND_VIOLATED; a satisfied partition has no reasons. An indeterminate partition has null accumulator and result with its explicit observation or time reason. The result includes full typed SET accumulators, not just their size.

Root status is VIOLATED if any partition is violated, otherwise INDETERMINATE if any is indeterminate, otherwise SATISFIED. Root reasons are the UTF-8 sorted unique union of partition reasons. Partition reasons are sorted unique. Every partition remains present even if another determines root status. Result fields are exactly schema, specification_pin, definition_digest, status, partitions and reasons. The schema token is `seampoint.work-class/1.0.0-draft.2/aggregate-result`; pin and definition identity bind the admitted inputs.

Admission applies these phases: (1) closed input shape; (2) manifest pin and definition identity; (3) definition/reference/order invariants; (4) type/literal/operand integrity throughout definitions and dynamic inputs; (5) projection, source/query/time/coverage/statistic integrity; (6) finite limits; (7) time and observation usability; (8) comparison. Every refusal in this candidate uses an empty path. Phase 1 returns SCHEMA_INVALID. A pin mismatch returns VERSION_UNSUPPORTED; a definition-digest mismatch returns INPUT_INVALID, with the pin checked first. Phase 3 returns REFERENCE_INVALID. Phase 4 returns TYPE_INVALID. Phase 5 returns INPUT_INVALID. Phase 6 returns LIMIT_EXCEEDED. A later result never masks an earlier failing phase. Within a phase all errors have the same code and path. No implementation-specific diagnostics enter the result.

Bounds are the common limits: 64 types and 64 mappings, 256 operations, 1024 members per collection, 128 numeric coefficient digits, depth 64 and 4096 predicate nodes across the definition. Digit-limit checks belong in phase 6 after lexical/type/integrity checks. Intermediate exact totals may grow beyond 128 digits, up to the mathematically necessary result of admitted inputs; output growth is not a reason to silently wrap or round. Referenced collection limits apply before duplicate collapse except observations and event snapshots, whose exact repeated records collapse before their limits are measured.

The dynamic validation matrix is normative. Phase 4 TYPE_INVALID covers every supplied value's scalar payload, nominal type, contribution-field compatibility, key-tuple types, qualifier operand types and statistic accumulator type. This includes operation fields, pending rows, ACTIVE event fields, statistic entries and SET elements. A missing required field, duplicate dynamic field name, unsorted dynamic inventory, missing/extra statistic key, a repeated pending key, or a pending/new occurrence collision is phase 5 INPUT_INVALID. Unknown definition-level type references, duplicate definitions/mapping IDs and invalid static ordering are phase 3 REFERENCE_INVALID. COUNT scalar accumulators and COUNT/CARDINALITY results are natural integers; SUM scalar accumulators/results are canonical nonnegative decimals; CARDINALITY accumulators are SETs of the exact element type. Output shape schemas cannot express every relation to an input definition, so passing an output shape check alone does not establish this matrix. Implementations must produce the required semantic output, and frozen expectations compare its complete bytes.

requirements.title: Readback and decisive evidence
requirements.observable_behavior:
Validation/readback admit the complete definition schema, identity/version, static references, literal/predicate semantics and limits. Definition schema is `seampoint.work-class/1.0.0-draft.2/aggregate-definition`. Readback uses common JSON-pointer leaf rendering over the whole definition, covering every operative field, including type, unit, window, source freshness and pending policy.

The worked sum has a complete committed accumulator of 800 USD, a bound LTE 1000 USD and a proposal of 150 USD, yielding 950 and SATISFIED. Two proposed 150 USD contributions in one partition yield 1100 and VIOLATED. With one earlier pending reservation of 150 USD, the remaining proposal also yields 1100. A CARDINALITY history containing B and C plus proposals A and B produces the set A,B,C and result 3. These judgments are arithmetic derivations; concrete fixture bytes and independently reviewed expectations must exist before they become conformance cases.

Source lineage: the selected Constraint Calculus 0.1.0 draft revision 15, sections 7, 8 and 14. This successor restates its reducers, grouping, exact arithmetic, temporal windows and observation distinctions directly. The scalar-key-element restriction, one-complete-bundle adapter, derived contribution projection and explicit pending policy are successor profile and encoding decisions requiring compatibility review. They do not establish that every source aggregate can be translated without loss. Composite-valued key elements, business-day calendars, signed netting and currency conversion remain visible requirements for later profiles. A grouping key may still contain several scalar elements under AGG-003.

requirements.title: Complete subjects and explicit limits
requirements.observable_behavior:
An authority input contains exactly the selected specification pin, source, work_class, envelope, proposal, clock, host_selection, occupancies, capacities, credentials, acts, returns and observations. `authority.schema.json` defines their closed fields. Every supplied record is complete. References do not fetch additional records. All arrays that name records sort by their unique id in UTF-8 byte order, except acts sort by canonical act digest and authenticated-record tuples sort by their complete canonical bytes. A duplicate inventory key is invalid even when the two bodies are identical. Source obligations, role lists, operation lists, required credential kinds, criterion identifiers and shared-budget anchors are sorted unique inventories.

The source has an id, revision and complete supplied obligation texts. The evaluator checks identities and declared obligation references; it does not interpret those texts or establish source completeness or fidelity. The work class has an id, revision, nominal scalar types and steps. Each step declares its operation, interface, executor role, exact named fields, subject/resource field coordinates and required credential kinds. Types and values have the aggregate contract's scalar semantics, scoped here by the complete work-class digest. Proposal fields are exactly the declared fields for its step, with exact nominal types. There is no omission default. The proposal binds the work-class digest and stable id, instance, occurrence, step, operation, interface, executor and all admitted fields. The first occurrence is explicit, such as `issue:1`; another instance or occurrence changes the proposal subject. The host must establish that these complete fields equal the actual native request.

Digest kinds are `authority-source`, `authority-work-class`, `authority-envelope`, `authority-proposal`, `authority-operation`, `authority-root`, `authority-capacity`, `authority-occupancy`, `authority-credential`, `authority-act`, `authority-return`, `authority-observation`, `authority-evidence` and `authority-result`. Each hashes the complete corresponding record under WCS2-002. None includes its own digest. The operation subject is exactly `{envelope_digest,work_class_digest,proposal_digest}`. Those complete dependencies are retained in the input; no policy-bearing proposal field is excluded.

The envelope binds its exact source and work-class digests, supporting obligation identifiers, responsible principal, grantor/executor/organizational-attester roles and expected grant act id. Its eight operative members are scope, operations, limits, conditions, enforcement, escalation, revocation and temporal_validity. Gate and unsupported limitations are additional required members. No role name supplies a missing member.

Scope contains an explicit scope id and nonempty subject/resource selector sets. CONSTANT copies a nonempty identity string; BINDING names one declared binding. A binding names its step, exact proposal field and IDENTITY or STRING type. It stores no instance value. Every binding applies to every envelope operation, so a parameterized envelope supports exactly one step. A constant-scope envelope may support several. The resolved scope is the sorted unique union of exact selector values. No normalization, case conversion or inferred requester identity occurs. Each step's scope_fields explicitly names the admitted proposal fields identifying its actual subjects and resources. They resolve to nonempty IDENTITY/STRING values, producing actual_scope. Every actual subject and resource must belong to the corresponding resolved grant set. A constant grant for card-A cannot authorize a native request for card-B merely because the returned receipt repeats card-A.

Operations are exact step/operation/interface triples, one per step, admitted against the supplied work class. Conditions are named predicates over the proposed step's admitted fields using AGG-003's complete FIELD/LITERAL predicate rules. All branches are type-checked, including false or unused branches. Each condition declares its applicable step. Observation-based general predicates, arbitrary callbacks and English conditions remain unsupported; a source requiring them must retain that limitation and cannot obtain readiness through a field-only substitute. Conditions on the time elapsed since another occurrence and freshness predicates on proposal fields are among them in this candidate.

Limits contain per_action numerical upper bounds and shared_budgets. A per-action bound names its step, field, exact typed nonnegative bound and LT or LTE; the referenced field is a nonnegative INTEGER or DECIMAL of the same nominal type. Every operation allowed by this envelope requires either a per-action upper bound or at least one declared shared-budget anchor. The latter remains an outstanding reservation obligation, not a satisfied authority check. The reservation consumer must establish every required anchor's coverage of this exact operation and jointly reserve its contribution before permission. A reference to an unrelated mapping or one that selects no contribution cannot satisfy that coverage requirement.

Enforcement declares mechanism identifiers, safe state and pre-actuation response. This profile supports only AUTHORITY_BEFORE_RESERVATION, ATOMIC_SHARED_RESERVATION when shared budgets occur, safe state NO_NEW_DISPATCH and response REFUSE. It records requirements for the runtime; the evaluator alone does not perform native enforcement. Escalation is DECLARED_NONE or a complete destination-role, authority-reference and decision-required record. A required escalation creates no implicit message or additional permission. Its runtime delivery remains unqualified unless a runtime profile supplies that transition. Nonempty limitations yield UNSUPPORTED_RELATION, preserving the source obligation rather than discarding it.

requirements.title: Gate and qualification policy
requirements.observable_behavior:
Gate records materiality LOW/MEDIUM/HIGH, reversibility HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW/NONE, kind NONE/VERIFY/DECIDE, role and named criteria. HIGH materiality or LOW/NONE reversibility requires DECIDE. Otherwise MEDIUM in either dimension requires at least VERIFY. Only LOW materiality with HIGH reversibility permits NONE. A stricter gate is valid. A non-NONE gate requires a role and at least one named criterion; NONE requires null role and no criteria. Gate criteria use the same closed field predicates and each applies to the exact selected operation. Unsupported imported criteria are limitations.

VERIFY is evidence under an existing grant. It cannot enlarge the scope, suppress a limit or supply a grant. DECIDE requires an actual per-instance decision and organizational attestation of that decision. Both retain the reusable grant and its separate attestation. Qualification by exact field predicates does not invent approval of every instance when the envelope declares NONE.

The grant is valid only within temporal_validity's explicit half-open interval: from inclusive, until exclusive; a null until explicitly declares no fixed end. A required revocation declaration supplies provider, source and nonnegative exact max_age_seconds. Root, capacities and credentials have their own independent revocation declarations. No interval substitutes for withdrawal evidence. All authority instants use whole-second UTC under WCS2-003. The clock source equals the envelope's declared clock_source. An unavailable clock cannot establish readiness.

requirements.title: Independently selected root and complete records
requirements.observable_behavior:
Host selection is a separate host-owned input. Its complete root binds the source, work class, envelope, principal, permitted capacity ids, occupancy ids, providers and channels. It has its own validity interval, revocation declaration, explicit prior_acts_survive_expiry flag, separation rule and empty-or-unsupported limitations. The host establishes the real designator, actual selection, authenticity and nonrollback history outside authoring. The selection_evidence reference identifies retained host evidence; its existence does not prove those facts.

Each channel names its provider, validity interval and explicit prior_returns_survive_expiry flag. A return must have occurred within that channel's interval. Current reliance requires an active channel or its explicit survival flag. Removing a historical channel without a retained permitted reliance record cannot silently authenticate its old return. Providers and channels are selected independently of the envelope author.

An occupancy binds id, actor, role, principal, HUMAN or MACHINE kind, validity interval, provider and evidence reference. A capacity binds those identities and occupancy to the exact root and envelope digests, permitted act kinds, its own validity, revocation and current-reliance terms. CURRENT_ONLY requires current capacity validity. SURVIVE_EXPIRY permits reliance on an act made during capacity validity only within its separately declared reliance interval. Silence establishes neither survival nor self-attestation permission. Authority acts require HUMAN occupancy; machines may execute. Synthetic research designations and proxies remain explicitly unsupported in this first direct-record profile. Synthetic test fixtures assert fictional host facts for apparatus tests and cannot be represented as real authority.

A credential binds its actor and occupancy to one step/operation/interface, credential kind, validity, provider, evidence and revocation declaration. Every required credential kind comes from the work class. An actor's credential cannot replace their occupancy, the grant, its attestation or a gate decision. Exactly one selected credential supplies each required kind; missing and conflicting selections fail rather than choosing first or last.

The host_selection.authenticated_records array contains exact `{kind,record_digest,provider,channel}` tuples for every supplied occupancy, capacity, credential and return, with null channel for non-return records. Each tuple binds the complete supplied record, and its provider/channel must occur in the selected root. No extra tuple is admitted. The root's complete record is separately selected through host_selection, avoiding a recursive claim that the root authenticates itself. Conformance tests these equalities, not authentication or organizational truth.

requirements.title: Acts, returns and historical authority
requirements.observable_behavior:
GRANT names the envelope digest and expected grant id, grantor role and responsible principal. ORGANISATIONAL_ATTESTATION names the canonical digest of one actual GRANT or INSTANCE_DECISION and its attested_actor. It uses the organizational-attester role and that same principal. VERIFY and INSTANCE_DECISION name the exact operation digest, use the gate role and name exactly the declared criterion ids. Grant and attestation criteria are empty. An attestation cannot attest another attestation.

Each act records id, kind, actor, role, principal, occupancy id, capacity id, recorder, occurred_at, disposition, subject_digest, attested_actor and criteria. ACCEPT alone can support readiness. REJECT, PENDING and DEFER remain evidence. Exactly one grant and one grant attestation are selected, plus the gate's required act and, for DECIDE, its attestation. Extra or competing selected acts are ACT_CONFLICT. Historical superseded or rejected acts remain outside this selected set; the host must not conceal a material conflict by selection, and this profile supplies no conflict-resolution or latest-wins rule.

The act's actor, role, principal and occupancy match its complete capacity and occupancy. The capacity permits that act kind and exact envelope. Both records are permitted by the root. Each act occurs within root, capacity and occupancy validity and no later than evaluation. Its attestation occurs no earlier than its decision; equality is allowed. No grant-before-gate ordering is added. A source requiring additional ordering must express it in supported policy or remain unsupported.

Self-attestation is permitted only if the attestation capacity's may_self_attest and the independently selected root's allow_self_attestation are both true. The direct authority evaluator implements no other separation relation within one authority input. The lifecycle may separately require that one exact `VERIFY` or `INSTANCE_DECISION` actor differ from an actor retained for an exact completed predecessor under LIFE-007. General separation formulas remain unsupported. Grantor, principal, executor, attester and recorder are not collapsed into one identity.

Every act has exactly one return containing its full canonical Base64 act bytes, act digest, actor, provider, channel and evidence reference. Decode original bytes under WCS2-001; the complete decoded act must equal the selected act. The return's record digest must be present in the independently supplied authenticated-record tuple. A bare act digest or successful tool submission is insufficient. This establishes an attributed supplied record under a declared host premise, not a cryptographic signature by the person.

requirements.title: Revocation observations and required checks
requirements.observable_behavior:
For every selected act derive root and capacity revocation checks at its occurrence and at current evaluation. Deduplicate identical query subjects/times. Also derive current envelope and required-credential revocation checks. A query is exactly `{purpose:"REVOCATION",subject_digest,at,provider,source}`; its digest kind is `authority-query`. Each observation carries this exact query and digest, status, as_of, revision, revoked value and evidence reference. AVAILABLE requires complete values; other statuses require null as_of/revision/revoked. Its provider must be permitted by the selected root. AVAILABLE as_of is no later than query.at and query.at minus as_of is at most the corresponding declaration's max_age_seconds. An AVAILABLE as_of later than query.at is a phase-1 date-validity failure, INPUT_INVALID; freshness is measured only for an as_of at or before query.at. This is an explicitly authored observation-freshness allowance, not an automatic guarantee that authority remains unchanged before dispatch.

The observation inventory contains exactly one row per derived query. Exact repeated rows collapse; distinct rows for one query produce AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED with OBSERVATION_CONFLICT. A missing row is EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE. An extra query or wrong query digest is DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH. UNAVAILABLE, INCOMPLETE, CONFLICT, stale or revoked observations cannot establish permission. Historical checks require their own exact historical query bindings; current observations cannot be relabelled as past evidence. Root/capacity expiry and withdrawal are separate. Root expiry permits current reliance on earlier acts only with prior_acts_survive_expiry; it never permits a new act outside its interval.

Derive the complete check set, never accept caller-authored SATISFIED rows. Checks cover exact work-class/proposal support, source/root bindings, scope substitution, materiality/gate floor, each per-action limit and condition, each selected act's occurrence-time capacity and occupancy, current reliance, root/capacity revocation at each required instant, current executor occupancy, every credential and its revocation, envelope validity/revocation, every gate criterion, return attribution and separation. Gate field criteria use the unchanged exact proposal at the gate's occurrence; independent time-varying facts need a later supported observation predicate contract. Shared-budget anchors are reported separately as unfulfilled requirements, never inserted as satisfied checks.

The result's checks use exact `{purpose,subject_digest,requirement_ref,at}` records sorted by their canonical bytes and deduplicated only when all fields are identical. Purpose tokens and construction are fixed in the schema companion inventory. The result binds the complete evidence bundle by `digest("authority-evidence",{host_selection,occupancies,capacities,credentials,acts,returns,observations,clock})`. No check claims to prove source English fidelity or the truth of host facts.

requirements.title: Refusal order and result
requirements.observable_behavior:
Apply these phases in order: (1) closed schema, canonical embedded bytes, scalar values, date validity and inventory ordering; (2) complete dependencies, identities and supported relations; (3) exact operation/field/executor/scope application and gate-floor checks; (4) selected act set, subjects, roles, dispositions, act-time records, returns and separation; (5) complete required observation inventory followed by current validity, freshness, revocation, conditions, limits and criteria; (6) construct readiness. A later policy outcome never hides earlier malformed input. Within a phase use the fixed code precedence in the schema companion; all refusals have empty path and a sorted reason list. The refusal includes no changed state because this evaluator is pure.

A successful result includes schema, specification_pin, status READY_FOR_RESERVATION, source/work-class/envelope/proposal/operation digests, resolved scope, actual_scope, selected act digests, complete satisfied check inventory, required_budgets and evidence_digest. The required_budgets list is the exact declared anchor set. Reservation must re-evaluate this complete input within its own atomic transition and satisfy those obligations against the same expected state revision. An old readiness receipt cannot be submitted as a replacement for the complete current authority input. Current revocation may prevent new admission; it does not make an already observed historical effect disappear.

## Compatibility boundary

No source requirement is silently replaced by a more restrictive per-instance approval or a weaker credential check.

The source binder's fully applicable result requires its limit consumers to have passed. This profile's readiness result deliberately stops before shared-budget checks. Only the combined reservation transition can supply the corresponding complete pre-dispatch judgment. Neither evaluator alone may claim that compatibility. Source confirmation, correspondence, organizational authorization of the artifact, production authentication and actual native mediation remain separately reviewed obligations.

requirements.title: Static definition admission
requirements.observable_behavior:

Validate/readback admit these complete bytes, not a detached envelope whose type and source dependencies are absent. Readback renders every scalar leaf and empty collection in this complete definition. A successful validate result hashes this definition; it does not establish a grant or ready a proposal.

All work-class types have AGG-001 scalar rules. Type/step/field identifiers are unique, and every declared field resolves to one type. Every envelope operation resolves to its exact work-class triple and executor role. The work class may declare additional steps outside this envelope; their existence grants no authority for them. A complete work runtime must establish their own applicable envelopes separately. Source and class digests are recomputed. All source_obligations resolve to supplied source identifiers. This proves correspondence of identifiers only; uncovered source meaning requires human review and cannot be discharged by code.

Each step's scope_fields.subjects and scope_fields.resources are sorted unique nonempty field-name lists. Every field resolves to a declared IDENTITY/STRING type. At application its value must be nonempty; the derived actual_scope lists are sorted unique. Actual subjects/resources must be subsets of the corresponding grant scope lists; failure is BINDING_MISMATCH. The result retains both scopes without changing the native proposal.

Bindings resolve against exact step/field declarations of IDENTITY or STRING kind; their values at application must be nonempty. Binding selectors resolve by id. Selector lists sort by canonical bytes and have no duplicate selector bodies. Constant scope and the union of substituted scope follow AUTH-001. Envelope operation rows sort by step. Condition, criterion and per-action limit rows sort by id; ids are unique within their respective collection. Every row's step occurs in envelope operations. A gate with VERIFY or DECIDE has at least one criterion for every permitted step; its selected act names exactly the criterion ids applicable to the proposed step. The complete per-step criterion inventory remains immutable in the envelope.

A FIELD operand resolves against that row's declared step and has its field's nominal type. Static literal types and all operand compatibility are checked even if another branch determines the predicate. A per-action bound's field and typed bound share one nonnegative numeric type. LT/LTE have their mathematical upper-bound meaning. Every envelope operation has at least one per-action bound or the envelope names shared budgets. An applicable shared budget must later select and reserve at least one contribution from that operation; declaring an unrelated anchor cannot complete the bound.

Materiality and gate requirements are checked at definition admission and again when applying the definition. A weaker gate is BINDING_MISMATCH. Required mechanisms are exactly `[AUTHORITY_BEFORE_RESERVATION]` without shared budgets, otherwise the UTF-8 sorted set `[ATOMIC_SHARED_RESERVATION,AUTHORITY_BEFORE_RESERVATION]`. Required escalation is retained policy; neither definition validation nor authority readiness asserts its delivery.

requirements.title: Record and time admission
requirements.observable_behavior:
Every complete interval has valid whole-second UTC endpoints, valid_from strictly before a nonnull valid_until. Null means explicitly unbounded above. All supplied dates are validated even in unused records. max_age_seconds is a natural integer with at most 128 digits. All nominal values are checked against the supplied class; unknown type references are REFERENCE_INVALID, malformed scalar values TYPE_INVALID. WCS2-004 finite collection, expression and number bounds also apply. Limits are checked after shape and scalar/reference integrity but before policy evaluation; they never cause wrapped arithmetic or a claimed policy refusal from a crash.

Root/source/class/envelope references match exact complete bytes. Each selected capacity binds that exact root/envelope. All supplied capacity and occupancy ids belong to the root's permitted inventories; every permitted id has exactly one supplied complete record. The authenticated-record tuples are exactly those derived from all supplied occupancy, capacity, credential and return records using their digest kind and provider/channel. Missing tuples or complete referenced bodies are EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE; extra or mismatched tuples are DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH. Every provider and return channel is selected by the root. Occupancy, capacity, credential and return record ids are unique within each collection; the same spelling in distinct record kinds is not an implicit relation.

Capacity act_kinds are a sorted unique list. Every selected act's capacity, occupancy, actor, role and principal match; capacity.root_digest and envelope_digest match complete selected records. Root and capacity principal equal envelope principal. The executor occupancy matches every executor field; executor role equals the envelope and work-class step role. Exactly the step's required credential kinds are selected, one record per kind, for that actor, occupancy and operation triple. Surplus credentials are DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH; missing required credentials are EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE. A supplied credential first binds its complete occupancy body: a different credential actor is a phase-2 DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH, and a missing occupancy body is EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE. Matching those complete records to the proposal executor and operation is phase 3. Credential and executor current intervals are checked at application, independently of old grant acts.

Returned_at is no earlier than its act's occurred_at and no later than the evaluation instant. Channel validity is tested at returned_at. Current channel reliance requires validity at evaluation or an explicit prior_returns_survive_expiry flag. A channel that fails this at evaluation is a phase-4 return-channel failure, so the refusal is ACT_NOT_AUTHORIZED with empty reasons and failed checks. Act-time root/capacity/occupancy checks do not use returned_at as a substitute. A current-root expiry does not erase old acts if the root explicitly permits survival; current withdrawal remains required. Occupancy expiry by itself does not erase an act made during valid occupancy; current capacity reliance determines continued use.

An unavailable clock still permits all directly checkable shape, dependency, static application and historical act checks. Omit comparisons against the missing current instant. In phase 5 return AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED with sole reason CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE before deriving current queries or checking their inventory. Wrong digest bodies, malformed supplied queries and date errors remain earlier failures. No machine-clock read fills the missing instant.

These symbols explain construction and are not wire fields. Every emitted check has exactly purpose, subject_digest, requirement_ref and at; successful readiness means all emitted checks were satisfied. There is no caller-supplied check array.

| Purpose | Subject | Requirement | Time |
|---|---|---|---|
| SOURCE_BINDING | E | source.id | now |
| ROOT_BINDING | E | root.id | now |
| INPUT_SUPPORT | O | proposal.step | now |
| BINDING | O | envelope.scope.id | now |
| GATE_FLOOR | E | envelope.id | now |
| ENVELOPE_VALIDITY | E | envelope.id | now |
| EXECUTOR_OCCUPANCY | O | executor.occupancy | now |
| CONDITION | O | each condition.id for proposal.step | now |
| PER_ACTION_LIMIT | O | each limit.id for proposal.step | now |
| CREDENTIAL | O | each required credential.id | now |
| ACT_CAPACITY | digest of each selected act | its capacity id | act.occurred_at |
| ACT_OCCUPANCY | digest of each selected act | its occupancy id | act.occurred_at |
| ACT_RELIANCE | digest of each selected act | its capacity id | now |

Root and each act's capacity are queried at every relevant act occurrence and at now. Envelope and selected credentials are queried at now. One exact subject/declaration/time query is required once even if several checks use it. Query digest uses the complete query under kind `authority-query`. Historical root or capacity withdrawal evidence concerns that historical instant. Current queries concern current reliance. The matching revocation declaration determines max_age; subjects cannot select a different allowance.

Observation arrays may arrive in any order. Collapse exact canonical duplicate rows. Different rows with the same query, including different evidence references, conflict; do not choose a revision by spelling or timestamp. Check the complete derived query inventory and all exact query digests before interpreting statuses. A missing query is EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE; an unrequested/mismatched query is DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH. Canonical revisions are opaque nonempty identifiers. No hidden state infers which revision is newer. Authentication, completeness and nonrollback choice are host responsibilities.

requirements.title: Deterministic refusal selection
requirements.observable_behavior:
Every refusal has exactly `{status:"REFUSED",code,path:"",reasons:[...],failed_checks:[...]}`. Phase order governs before the following within-phase code orders. Accumulate directly checkable failures within the phase and select its first code; do not let loop order choose a different result.

1. SCHEMA_INVALID, ARTIFACT_ENCODING_INVALID, ARTIFACT_NONCANONICAL, TYPE_INVALID, INPUT_INVALID. This includes every embedded return's bytes and schema. Duplicate/sort inventory errors are INPUT_INVALID. Type-reference resolution is deferred to phase 2 when necessary to distinguish a missing declaration from a malformed known value.
2. VERSION_UNSUPPORTED, DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH, EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, UNSUPPORTED_RELATION, REFERENCE_INVALID, LIMIT_EXCEEDED. Version is checked first; complete digest bindings precede unsupported relations. An id cannot stand in for its missing body.
3. BINDING_MISMATCH. Exact field inventory, declared types at application, operation matching, scope substitution and materiality floor are application checks.
4. ACT_CONFLICT, GATE_REQUIRED, EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, ACT_NOT_AUTHORIZED, ACT_NOT_ACCEPTED. Extra/competing selected acts precede missing gate evidence; missing other required acts/returns/bodies follow. Subject, principal, role, capacity, occupancy, act-time validity, return-channel and separation failures are ACT_NOT_AUTHORIZED. A selected non-ACCEPT disposition is ACT_NOT_ACCEPTED. Check inventories by expected act role/subject so swapped identities cannot masquerade as absent records.
5. DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH, EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE, AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED. Resolve observation inventory before dispositions. CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE has the special early treatment above. For other AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED results, reasons are the sorted unique union of all failed current/historical revocation, current validity, condition, per-action limit and gate-criterion checks. The enum in the schema fixes reason spelling. Missing current validity or withdrawal is never a default pass.

Reasons are empty for every code except AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED. ACT_EXPIRED and CAPACITY_EXPIRED are reserved reason tokens and are not emitted for phase-4 act-time refusals, whose reasons remain empty. Current credential expiry uses CREDENTIAL_EXPIRED, envelope expiry ENVELOPE_EXPIRED, executor occupancy expiry ACT_EXPIRED, current capacity reliance failure RELIANCE_EXPIRED, current root expiry without survival ROOT_EXPIRED, unavailable/incomplete/conflicting/stale observations their named reason, and a true revoked value REVOKED. False field predicates and exceeded bounds use CONDITION_VIOLATED, GATE_CRITERION_VIOLATED or PER_ACTION_LIMIT_VIOLATED. Contradictory observations suppress interpreting either revoked value for that query; retain OBSERVATION_CONFLICT.

`failed_checks` records how an AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED refusal was decided. It has one row `{purpose,subject_digest,requirement_ref,at,reason}` for every reason a failed phase-5 check contributed. `purpose`, `subject_digest`, `requirement_ref` and `at` are exactly the values the Exact successful check construction table assigns to that check, and `reason` is that reason; a check that contributed two reasons, such as an observation that is both stale and revoked, has two rows with equal check values. A current root expiry without survival is reported against the `ROOT_BINDING` check. Rows sort by canonical bytes and are unique, and the set of their reasons equals `reasons`. `failed_checks` is empty for every other code and for the CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE refusal, which evaluates no check.

Digest-domain selection is a semantic rule. All authority digest kinds are listed in AUTH-001, supplemented by authority-query in AUTH-005 and authority-definition here. A digest-shaped string alone does not validate either the subject bytes or the selected domain. The schema intentionally owns syntax while these rules own recomputation.

requirements.title: Choice routing
requirements.observable_behavior:
A choice record contains:

```json
{
  "step_id": "route",
  "label_type_ref": "route-label",
  "label_values": [
    {"type_ref": "route-label", "value": "APPROVE"},
    {"type_ref": "route-label", "value": "REJECT"}
  ]
}
```

A choice has exactly one source step, one label type and a finite list of allowed typed values. The step's completion carrier identifies the label field. Its `LABEL` relationships provide the complete label map. Every allowed value appears exactly once, and every label edge targets one step. An ordinary `SEQUENCE` edge cannot coexist with label edges on the same choice step. A declared `FAILURE` relationship is separate from the success label map.

The label is read from `route_label_field` in the exact native record of a matching terminal `EFFECT_OBSERVED` event. The proposal cannot carry a route label. A dispatch observation cannot carry one. The lifecycle does not use a default label, a language model, a connector status or a process-local value. If the terminal effect's label is absent, unknown, duplicated, or fails the declared type, the effect record is retained and the lifecycle admits `STOPPED` with `LABEL_INVALID`. No successor is active.

The static definition is inadmissible when a route is missing, duplicated, ambiguously typed, or points outside the definition. A schema-admitted choice whose label domain lacks one exact target is `DEFINITION_INVALID`. A reference to an undeclared target is `REFERENCE_INVALID`. A static mapping error is an input refusal at validation or deployment. It is separate from an invalid label observed at runtime.

Every completion, routing, expiry and obligation-discharge rule below applies only after `LIFECYCLE.md` classifies the occurrence and event as eligible to progress. A `BLOCKED_DISPUTE`, closed, late, unknown, unexpected, foreign, conflicting or budget-disputed case retains evidence and reconciles exposure under the lifecycle rule without applying a normal composition route, except where that rule states a specific evidence-only state change.

A matching terminal success effect at a choice step supplies exactly one value at the declared label field. The consumer validates the value against the closed label type and looks up the exact route. It records the native effect, the selected label, and the relationship in the same atomic transition that completes the occurrence. It activates the selected target only. Unselected targets never become obligations.

A terminal failure effect uses the source step's declared failure relationship. The relationship is absent exactly when that step declares `STOP`. The consumer does not treat a failure as a success label and does not select a route from an incomplete or unknown effect.

An observed invalid label is a runtime policy stop. The transition retains the full terminal effect, actuation identity, reservation treatment, label extraction result and error reason. It returns `STOPPED` with `LABEL_INVALID`, leaves no successor active, and prevents new scheduling under the declared stop semantics. The state remains reviewable and the effect is not converted into a refusal.

requirements.title: Bounded loops
requirements.observable_behavior:
This candidate admits bounded simple loops through explicit loop records. A loop record contains `id`, `entry_step_id`, the complete sorted set of `member_step_ids`, `back_edge_from_step_id`, and positive `maximum_passes`. Its one back edge is the relationship from `back_edge_from_step_id` to `entry_step_id`. The loop member set must equal one cyclic strongly connected component in the normalized relationship graph. Every cycle in that component must cross the declared entry and the one back edge. Loop member sets cannot overlap or nest in this candidate. An undeclared cycle, another back edge, a cycle that bypasses the entry, or a cross-loop edge is `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`.

Pass one begins when the entry is first activated from outside the loop. Taking the declared back edge increments the pass. Every operation occurrence in the loop carries one `LOOP` enclosing segment with the loop identifier and current pass; branch and fan-out segments remain in their outer-to-inner positions. Activation beyond `maximum_passes` is a retained `STOPPED/LOOP_BOUND_REACHED` decision and creates no new occurrence. Every recurring step also has a positive `occurrence_limit`. Activation at that step maximum is allowed; the next activation is a retained `STOPPED/LIMIT_EXCEEDED` decision. These checks occur in complete structural preflight before any successor or obligation is created.

The loop record and graph must agree exactly. The entry belongs to `member_step_ids`; the named back-edge source belongs to that set; exactly one declared relationship runs from that source to the entry; and no other relationship inside the component returns to the entry. Entry from outside allocates pass `1`. A relationship inside the loop preserves the current pass, and selecting the one back edge allocates current pass plus one. An edge leaving the loop removes its segment. Since loop member sets cannot overlap or nest, the current loop pass is one plus the largest retained pass for the pair `(loop_id, exact outer enclosing prefix)` only when the back edge is selected; a new outer branch or object context begins at one. The state therefore needs no process-local loop counter.

An occurrence ordinal is one plus the largest retained ordinal for that step across the work instance, or one when no occurrence of the step exists. Root ordinal is one. Parallel-block and fan-out pass numbers are one plus the largest retained pass for the pair `(construct_id, exact outer enclosing prefix)`, or one on first entry in that context. All ordinals and passes use exact natural-integer arithmetic. When one transition activates several branch or fan-out occurrences, allocate them in declared source order after preflighting the complete set. Their persisted values cannot depend on worker order or process memory.

`maximum_activations` counts all created proposal-capable occurrences, including root, loop, branch and fan-out occurrences; structural nodes do not count. The corresponding total and per-step activation counters increment at occurrence creation. `maximum_actuations` counts initial `PERMITTED` proposals and increments only when the first permit and any required reservation commit for an occurrence. Renewing an expired, undispatched permit does not create another actuation and does not increment this counter. An initial proposal that would exceed the limit records `STOPPED/LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, creates no permit or reservation and leaves the registry unchanged. A higher work-class maximum cannot override a step occurrence or loop-pass maximum.

Static admission requires a positive root occurrence limit, a positive `maximum_activations`, and values within WCS2-004. `maximum_actuations`, `maximum_active_obligations`, and `maximum_fanout_objects` may be zero because a valid work class may deliberately admit no actuation, no concurrent obligation, or only an empty fan-out. Initial-proposal preflight checks `maximum_actuations` after authority succeeds and before evaluating a cloned reservation transition. A failure records `STOPPED` with a `LIMIT` detail of kind `ACTUATIONS`; the authority result remains retained, while no permit, reservation or registry receipt is created.

When one atomic closure would cross several limits, the one `LIMIT` detail uses this precedence: `STEP_OCCURRENCES`, `LOOP_PASSES`, `ACTIVATIONS`, `ACTIVE_OBLIGATIONS`, then `FANOUT_OBJECTS`. `ACTUATIONS` applies only during proposal preflight and therefore does not compete with a structural closure. The detail records the selected declared limit, the projected count that would result, and the applicable step or relationship. All crossed limits may remain visible in implementation diagnostics, but they do not change the canonical decision.

Structural preflight uses this first-failure order: per-step occurrence maximum, loop pass maximum, total activation maximum, active-obligation maximum, then fan-out object maximum. It computes the complete union before creating a successor. Active or unresolved obligations are those with status `OPEN`, `BLOCKED`, `WAITING` or `DISPUTED`; discharged or joined obligations do not count. `maximum_fanout_objects` applies to each frozen expansion set, while `maximum_active_obligations` bounds the instance-wide concurrent inventory. If several records fail the same limit, the detail identifies the first proposed activation in declared relationship, branch, deadline, or object source order. The triggering effect and reservation settlement commit, its occurrence closes, zero successor occurrences or obligations from the failed closure are created, and the instance becomes `STOPPED`. The `LIMIT` detail records the kind, declared limit, projected value, source step and selected relationship digest when present.

A proposal retry with the same event identity is exact replay and changes no counter. A new occurrence requires a fresh proposal, current authority evaluation, current credential and observation bindings, and current reservation evaluation. Authority for occurrence one does not authorize occurrence two. The persisted counters survive restart and are covered by state identity.

A conforming suite includes every declared label, success and failure route, missing and unknown observed label, duplicate static mapping, a loop activation at its exact maximum, the next attempted activation, an earlier actuation limit, exact replay, altered replay and foreign completion. Every case includes the complete next state and retained evidence.

requirements.title: Prior-effect and actor bindings
requirements.observable_behavior:
A proposal-capable step may declare `prior_effect_bindings` and `prior_actor_separations`. Both arrays sort by record identifier in raw UTF-8 order and reject duplicate identifiers. Two prior-effect bindings on one step cannot name the same target request field. Structural steps require both arrays to be empty. These records express dependencies on retained governed history; they do not extend an authority envelope across steps.

A prior-effect binding has exactly `id`, `selection`, `source_step_id`, `source_evidence_field` and `target_request_field`. This candidate supports only `UNIQUE_COMPLETED_ANCESTOR`. The source and target are proposal-capable steps. The source step has a completion carrier whose evidence bindings contain the source evidence field exactly once, and that row binds it to exactly one source request field. The target request field occurs exactly once on the declaring step. The source request field and target request field have the same nominal `type_ref`, and the referenced type declaration is a supported scalar type. Missing steps or fields are `REFERENCE_INVALID`; a structural source or target, different types, a duplicate identifier or target, or an ineligible completion field is `DEFINITION_INVALID`.

A prior-actor separation has exactly `id`, `relation`, `selection`, `prior_step_id`, `prior_act_kind` and `current_act_kind`. This candidate supports only `DISTINCT_ACTOR` and `UNIQUE_COMPLETED_ANCESTOR`; the act kinds are `VERIFY` and `INSTANCE_DECISION`. The prior and current steps are proposal-capable and each declares one authority requirement. This work-class check cannot prove what a separately supplied authority envelope will select. LIFE-007 checks the exact selected acts at proposal time.

For both record kinds, the selected source must be in the recursive predecessor closure of the current occurrence. It must be a completed occurrence for the declared source step with disposition `SUCCEEDED`, established by exactly one retained governed `MATCHED` outcome that is not disputed and whose native-evidence digest equals the completed occurrence's evidence digest. Zero eligible occurrences, including a source whose establishing outcome is now disputed, is `PREREQUISITE_MISSING`; more than one is `BINDING_MISMATCH`. The consumer does not choose by time, ordinal, array position or graph distance. Another instance, a sibling path and any occurrence outside the predecessor closure are ineligible.

requirements.title: Conformance obligations
requirements.observable_behavior:
A composition implementation claiming `CHOICE_LOOP_RUNTIME` MUST pass the complete linear and choice/loop cases. A `DEADLINE_RUNTIME` claim also requires every lower-profile case and the clock/deadline cases. A `PARALLEL_FANOUT_RUNTIME` claim requires all prior cases and the block/fan-out cases. Capabilities cannot claim a profile whose static, transition, state, replay or host tests are absent.

The suite compares complete canonical decisions, receipts, state and digests. It includes exact replay, altered replay, stale state, foreign subjects, invalid route labels, limit stops, late effects, state restart, generated inputs, state interchange and mutations. A pure graph validator does not qualify the lifecycle runtime. A state transition pass does not qualify serialized contention. A single-process host pass does not qualify durable or distributed enforcement.

requirements.title: Activity deadlines
requirements.observable_behavior:
`DEADLINES` adds a persisted deadline to an active operation occurrence. The profile uses the clock and event rules in `LIFECYCLE.md`.

### 5.1 Deadline definition

A deadline record contains:

```json
{
  "id": "deadline-1",
  "step_id": "review",
  "due": {
    "kind": "ELAPSED_DURATION",
    "value": "60",
    "unit": "MINUTE"
  },
  "clock_source": "clock-1",
  "boundary": "AT_OR_AFTER",
  "expiry_target": "escalate"
}
```

The definition's `due` declaration is an exact UTC `ABSOLUTE_INSTANT`, an exact positive `ELAPSED_DURATION`, or an exact positive `ELAPSED_FROM_ANCESTOR` with `value`, `unit` and `anchor_step_id`. An elapsed declaration is added to the admitted activation instant. An ancestor declaration is added to the `occurred_at` instant of the anchor occurrence, which is the one completed occurrence of `anchor_step_id` in the recursive predecessor closure of the occurrence the deadline activates with. Either result is the absolute instant persisted in the deadline-state field `due`. Static admission requires an ancestor declaration's anchor to be a proposal-capable step other than the deadline's own step, not a member of any loop, not inside a fan-out region that does not also contain the deadline's step, and on every path from the root to the deadline's step in the normalized graph; together these make the anchor occurrence exist and be unique at every activation. A declaration that fails any of them, including one on the root step, is `DEFINITION_INVALID`; an undeclared anchor step is `REFERENCE_INVALID`. The profile supports `AT_OR_AFTER` and `AFTER` only. A proposal-capable step has at most one deadline, so one occurrence cannot select competing expiry routes. A deadline has exactly one expiry relationship or an explicit stop result. It cannot infer a target from a step name.

`expiry_target` is nonnull exactly when there is one `EXPIRY` relationship whose `from` equals the deadline step, whose `to` equals that target and whose `deadline_ref` equals the deadline ID. A null target means explicit stop and requires no such relationship. Another, duplicate or mismatched expiry edge is `DEFINITION_INVALID` or `REFERENCE_INVALID` as applicable.

A deadline is activated with its operation occurrence. The closed state record stores `deadline_id`, `occurrence_id`, `activation_digest`, `trigger_digest`, `source`, `activation_revision`, `activation_clock_revision`, `activation_instant`, `activation_clock_evidence_digest`, `due`, `boundary`, `status` and nullable `expiry_event_digest`, exactly as LIFE-014 and `lifecycle.schema.json` define them. Restart uses this persisted record. It does not recalculate `due` from the current clock or local timezone.

The candidate excludes business-day, holiday, fiscal-calendar, provider SLA and implicit local-time rules. Aggregate calendar windows are a separate aggregate feature and do not supply deadline semantics.

### 5.2 Clock and expiry

Only an admitted `CLOCK` event updates the accepted lifecycle clock. A clock event identifies its declared source and revision. An available sample whose revision is greater than the stored revision updates the clock. A stale or backward revision is refused. An unavailable or conflicting sample is an admitted retained fact with `CLOCK_UNAVAILABLE` and cannot establish expiry.

After accepting an available clock, the consumer evaluates every active deadline whose predicate is satisfied. It orders simultaneous expiry records by due instant, complete occurrence identity and deadline ID. For an eligible non-`BLOCKED_DISPUTE` occurrence, the expiry record removes the occurrence from dispatchable active work, retains the clock and deadline evidence, and follows the declared expiry relationship or stop result. For a dependency-blocked occurrence, the deadline becomes `EXPIRED` as evidence while the occurrence and obligation remain blocked; no expiry route or stop is applied. LIFE-014 defines the mixed due-set transition.

`AT_OR_AFTER` is satisfied when the accepted clock's `observed_time >= deadline_state.due`. `AFTER` is satisfied only when `observed_time > deadline_state.due`. A clock exactly at an `AT_OR_AFTER` `due` instant expires an eligible occurrence or records evidence-only expiry for a dependency-blocked occurrence. A clock exactly at an `AFTER` `due` instant does not.

Completion and expiry are ordered by admitted event sequence. A terminal effect admitted before the expiry transition completes the occurrence. A later clock event cannot expire it. A clock event admitted first expires the occurrence. A later effect is late evidence and cannot rewind the route, even if the provider event time precedes the due instant. The effect time remains available for review and reservation settlement.

Expiry does not release a reservation. Pending dispatch, unknown effect, and unsettled reservation records remain retained. Timeout, revocation, and permit expiry do not satisfy the affirmative no-effect evidence and organizational authorization required for release.

### 5.3 Deadline cases

A conforming suite includes one instant before due, exactly due and one instant after for both predicates, an unavailable clock, a conflicting sample, a stale revision, wrong source, replay, completion before expiry, a late effect after expiry, an unknown effect retained after expiry, and restart preserving the persisted due instant.
