requirements.title: Definition contract
requirements.observable_behavior:
A work-class definition contains these semantic groups. The JSON Schema gives each group a closed object shape and rejects undeclared fields.

| Group | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| Identity | Candidate pin, work-class identity, revision, profile, root and source references. The definition digest is computed from the complete canonical definition. |
| Participants | Declared participant identities, roles and kinds. Exact actor and credential bindings arrive with each proposal. |
| Objects | Declared object identities and types available to the work class. |
| Steps | Step identity, operation kind, fields, executor role, credentials, authority requirements, budgets, prior-effect field bindings, cross-occurrence actor separation, dispatch-permit duration and completion carrier. |
| Relationships | Ordered, typed graph edges with exact source and target. |
| Choices | Closed label type, completion-carrier source field and total label-edge mapping. |
| Loops and occurrence limits | Explicit bounded simple loops, per-step occurrence maxima and work-class proposal, activation and actuation maxima. |
| Deadlines | Deadline identity, active step, due rule, clock source, boundary and expiry target. |
| Blocks | Structured parallel split, branches, join and ancestry rules. |
| Fan-outs | Expand step, typed source field, region, join, object key and empty-set behavior. |
| Authority and budgets | Exact authority requirement and shared-budget identities. Their complete definitions and records use their own candidate schemas. |
| Source correspondence | The source identity, revision and obligation identifiers that the separate evidence records bind to the work class. |

The definition's graph and all referenced types are self-contained in the candidate's bundled schema graph. References are inert identifiers. They do not cause filesystem, network or repository access.

Definition inventories have unique semantic keys. Participant, object, type, step, loop, deadline, parallel-block and fan-out identifiers are unique. Choice and occurrence-limit records are unique by step. At most one deadline names a step. A step cannot be owned by two choices. A proposal-capable step cannot be a direct member of two sibling branch regions, two sibling fan-out regions or two non-ancestor structured constructs. Nested membership is permitted: the innermost branch or object region directly owns its proposal-capable steps, while each enclosing construct remains represented in occurrence ancestry and its obligation waits on the exact child pass. Structural split and join nodes form the boundary through which the parent region enters and leaves that child construct. Every proposal-capable step in a fan-out object region, including a nested child construct, contains the object-request field declared by each enclosing fan-out, with the corresponding object type. Those field names are distinct along one nested fan-out path. Participants, objects, types, steps, choices, occurrence limits, loops, deadlines, parallel blocks and fan-outs sort by their identifier or step key in raw UTF-8 order; the top-level shared-budget list and each identifier-valued set use the same order. Step fields sort by name. Relationships, choice label values and parallel branches retain declared source order and reject canonical duplicates. A fan-out pass that creates object occurrences also retains source order and rejects canonical duplicate object keys. The one `FANOUT_SET_DUPLICATE` policy-stop form defined by FAN-001 instead retains the complete duplicate source array, creates no occurrences or obligations and remains admissible on restart as evidence of the stop. Static validation rejects every other duplicate or out-of-order canonical inventory before graph evaluation.

### 2.1 Normalized relationship form

Every admitted relationship has one of four closed forms. Array order is source order. For example:

```json
{
  "kind": "SEQUENCE",
  "from": "review",
  "to": "publish"
}
```

The forms are `SEQUENCE`, `FAILURE`, `LABEL`, and `EXPIRY`. A `SEQUENCE`, `FAILURE`, or `LABEL` relationship is selected only by the corresponding terminal effect evidence. A `LABEL` relationship also carries one typed label. An `EXPIRY` relationship carries its deadline reference and is selected only by that deadline transition. A parallel or fan-out join uses its declared sequence edge only after the exact obligation inventory is discharged. A fan-out empty-set transition follows the construct's declared behavior.

A relationship has exactly one source, one target and one kind. Label and deadline fields exist only on their respective variants. A relationship cannot be selected by a proposal, dispatch observation, provider callback, or missing evidence. A consumer MUST reject duplicate canonical relationship records and ambiguous relationships before deployment.

The source order is retained in canonical form and in readback. It is used for deterministic evaluation when several independent records become eligible in one transition. A consumer MUST NOT sort source-defined arrays by a local map order or locale.

The normalized graph contains every declared relationship plus two kinds of construct edge. Each parallel block contributes one ordered edge from its split to each branch head. Each fan-out contributes one edge from its expand step to its region head. A branch or fan-out region reaches its declared join through an explicit relationship from each possible region tail; no implicit tail edge is supplied. Reachability and strongly connected component checks use this combined graph. A branch region is the set reachable from its head without crossing its block join or a sibling branch head. A fan-out region is the set reachable from its head without crossing its join. A nested child construct is treated as one structured subgraph for direct ownership: its split or expand boundary belongs to the parent path, its inner proposal-capable steps belong directly to the child regions, and its join returns to the parent path. Every path through either parent or child region must reach that region's declared join. Two regions may overlap only by strict nesting through those boundaries; partial overlap or entry into a child region anywhere except its split or expand boundary is `DEFINITION_INVALID`. Static admission rejects a graph that can produce an occurrence with more than 64 enclosing loop, branch or fan-out segments. This same bound limits the construct identifiers traversed by one structural closure. These rules determine direct ownership, ancestor membership, cross-boundary refusals and loop containment without inferring structure from step names.

Outgoing and construct edges obey this complete matrix:

| Source step or construct | Required and permitted edges |
|---|---|
| Ordinary `OPERATION` without a choice | exactly one `SEQUENCE` success edge; one `FAILURE` edge exactly when `failure_behavior` is `FAILURE_EDGE`; no `LABEL` edge |
| `OPERATION` with a choice | no `SEQUENCE` success edge; exactly one `LABEL` edge for every declared label value; one `FAILURE` edge exactly when `failure_behavior` is `FAILURE_EDGE` |
| `FANOUT_EXPAND` | exactly one fan-out construct names it; no `SEQUENCE` or `LABEL` success edge; one `FAILURE` edge exactly when `failure_behavior` is `FAILURE_EDGE` |
| `PARALLEL_SPLIT` | exactly one parallel block names it; its branch heads come only from that block's ordered implicit edges; it has no explicit outgoing relationship |
| `PARALLEL_JOIN` or `FANOUT_JOIN` | exactly one matching construct names it and exactly one outgoing `SEQUENCE` relationship selects its successor, which may be `TERMINAL`; it has no other outgoing relationship |
| `TERMINAL` | no outgoing relationship and no construct edge |
| Deadline on a proposal-capable step | at most one deadline names the step; it contributes exactly one `EXPIRY` edge when `expiry_target` is nonnull and none when expiry stops |

A parallel split has exactly one explicit incoming relationship from outside its block. A parallel branch head has only its block's implicit incoming edge, except for an admitted back edge wholly inside that branch. A fan-out region head has only its fan-out's implicit incoming edge, except for an admitted back edge wholly inside that object region. A parallel or fan-out join receives explicit relationships only from tails in its own region; every possible region path reaches that join. Ordinary operations, fan-out expand steps and terminal steps may have several incoming relationships when the closed choice, loop or structured graph rules distinguish them. A duplicate edge, an extra construct owner, an incoming cross-boundary edge or a cardinality outside this table is `DEFINITION_INVALID`; an undeclared endpoint is `REFERENCE_INVALID`.

### 2.2 Step records

A step record contains, at minimum:

```json
{
  "id": "review",
  "kind": "OPERATION",
  "executor_role": "reviewer",
  "interface": "review-service",
  "operation": "record-review",
  "fields": [{"name": "record-id", "type_ref": "identity"}],
  "scope_fields": {"subjects": ["record-id"], "resources": ["record-id"]},
  "required_credentials": ["reviewer-credential"],
  "authority_requirements": ["review-authority"],
  "shared_budgets": [],
  "prior_effect_bindings": [],
  "prior_actor_separations": [],
  "permit_seconds": "300",
  "failure_behavior": "FAILURE_EDGE",
  "completion": {
    "effect_provider": "review-provider",
    "effect_source": "review-service",
    "effect_record_type": "review-result",
    "no_effect_provider": "review-provider",
    "no_effect_source": "review-service",
    "no_effect_record_type": "review-no-effect",
    "status_field": "status",
    "status_type_ref": "status",
    "success_values": [{"type_ref": "status", "value": "ACCEPTED"}],
    "failure_values": [{"type_ref": "status", "value": "REJECTED"}],
    "route_label_field": null,
    "route_label_type_ref": null,
    "evidence_bindings": [
      {"request_field": "record-id", "evidence_field": "record-id"}
    ]
  }
}
```

The exact schema defines fields, credentials, authority, budgets, prior-history requirements and completion carriers. A `PARALLEL_SPLIT`, `PARALLEL_JOIN`, `FANOUT_JOIN`, or `TERMINAL` step is structural: it has null executor, interface, operation, scope fields, permit duration, failure behavior and completion fields and is never proposed or dispatched. It also has empty credential, authority, shared-budget, prior-effect and prior-actor arrays. An `OPERATION` or `FANOUT_EXPAND` step is proposal-capable and has nonnull executor, interface, operation, scope fields, failure behavior and completion fields. It also declares a positive `permit_seconds` value. That finite duration fixes how long the organization accepts proposal-time authority and observation snapshots for native dispatch. No implementation default supplies it. Scope fields contain sorted, unique, nonempty subject and resource field-name lists and follow the direct-authority meaning in `AUTHORITY.md`. A `FANOUT_EXPAND` completion carrier supplies the declared object collection; every other proposal-capable step requires `native_evidence.collections:[]`. An operation step has a complete, closed operation input contract. It cannot invoke another work class in this candidate. The root must be proposal-capable. A proposal-capable step carries exactly one authority requirement in this candidate. That identifier equals the complete authority input's envelope identifier. The envelope may require many checks, acts, observations and shared budgets; the one work-class identifier does not reduce that inventory. The definition's top-level `shared_budgets` is the raw UTF-8 sorted unique union of every proposal-capable step's shared-budget list, with no unused or omitted anchor. A proposal-capable step completes by routing to another proposal-capable step or to a structural node; a `TERMINAL` structural node has no outgoing relationship. The source obligation list is nonempty because every proposal must project the complete source obligation set into its authority input.

Every completion carrier declares exact `effect_provider`, `effect_source`, `effect_record_type`, `no_effect_provider`, `no_effect_source`, `no_effect_record_type`, `status_field` and `status_type_ref` values; every success and failure value has that exact scalar type. An established or unknown effect uses the effect triple. An affirmative no-effect record uses the no-effect triple. The selected triple must equal the corresponding native-evidence fields before the consumer interprets a result. The two triples may differ; neither is inferred from the other. `route_label_field` and `route_label_type_ref` are either both null or both nonnull. They are nonnull exactly for a declared choice, and the type equals that choice's `label_type_ref`. The carrier's status field, nonnull route-label field and evidence-field names are pairwise distinct. Each evidence field inherits the scalar type of its uniquely bound native request field. The success and failure arrays are canonical sets and are disjoint. The evidence bindings contain each native request field exactly once on the request side and use unique evidence field names. A missing or inconsistent reference is `REFERENCE_INVALID`; overlapping success and failure values, duplicate field names or bindings, an incomplete mapping, or a typed value that disagrees with its declared type is `DEFINITION_INVALID`. These declarations form the complete native completion-field contract; no ambient connector schema is needed to interpret a carrier. An operation's `failure_behavior` is `FAILURE_EDGE` exactly when it has one outgoing `FAILURE` relationship, and is `STOP` exactly when it has none. More than one failure edge is invalid. This step rule is the sole failure-policy declaration for choices and operations inside parallel or fan-out regions.

A matched effect performs the finite structural closure reachable from its selected relationship in that same lifecycle transition. Reaching a `PARALLEL_SPLIT` atomically creates its declared branch obligations and proposal-capable branch heads. Reaching a `PARALLEL_JOIN` or `FANOUT_JOIN` advances only when its exact retained obligations are discharged. Reaching a `TERMINAL` completes the instance. Static admission rejects a structural chain, structural cycle or structural target that would require another external event. An admitted effect whose structural closure would exceed a declared occurrence, activation, obligation or fan-out limit is retained and produces `STOPPED` with reason `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`; none of that closure's successor occurrences or obligations is created. Actuation limits are checked at proposal because structural closure creates no permit. This rule introduces no fifth lifecycle event.

An occurrence limit is a separate record containing a step identity and an exact nonnegative integer string. A limit is per work instance and step unless a containing construct explicitly declares a narrower scope. The work-class maximum actuation count is separate and cannot raise any step occurrence limit.

### 2.3 Prior-effect and actor bindings

A proposal-capable step may declare `prior_effect_bindings` and `prior_actor_separations`. Both arrays sort by record identifier in raw UTF-8 order and reject duplicate identifiers. Two prior-effect bindings on one step cannot name the same target request field. Structural steps require both arrays to be empty. These records express dependencies on retained governed history; they do not extend an authority envelope across steps.

A prior-effect binding has exactly `id`, `selection`, `source_step_id`, `source_evidence_field` and `target_request_field`. This candidate supports only `UNIQUE_COMPLETED_ANCESTOR`. The source and target are proposal-capable steps. The source step has a completion carrier whose evidence bindings contain the source evidence field exactly once, and that row binds it to exactly one source request field. The target request field occurs exactly once on the declaring step. The source request field and target request field have the same nominal `type_ref`, and the referenced type declaration is a supported scalar type. Missing steps or fields are `REFERENCE_INVALID`; a structural source or target, different types, a duplicate identifier or target, or an ineligible completion field is `DEFINITION_INVALID`.

A prior-actor separation has exactly `id`, `relation`, `selection`, `prior_step_id`, `prior_act_kind` and `current_act_kind`. This candidate supports only `DISTINCT_ACTOR` and `UNIQUE_COMPLETED_ANCESTOR`; the act kinds are `VERIFY` and `INSTANCE_DECISION`. The prior and current steps are proposal-capable and each declares one authority requirement. This work-class check cannot prove what a separately supplied authority envelope will select. LIFE-007 checks the exact selected acts at proposal time.

For both record kinds, the selected source must be in the recursive predecessor closure of the current occurrence. It must be a completed occurrence for the declared source step with disposition `SUCCEEDED`, established by exactly one retained governed `MATCHED` outcome that is not disputed and whose native-evidence digest equals the completed occurrence's evidence digest. Zero eligible occurrences, including a source whose establishing outcome is now disputed, is `PREREQUISITE_MISSING`; more than one is `BINDING_MISMATCH`. The consumer does not choose by time, ordinal, array position or graph distance. Another instance, a sibling path and any occurrence outside the predecessor closure are ineligible.

### 2.4 Choice records

A choice record contains:

```json
{
  "step_id": "route",
  "label_type_ref": "route-label",
  "label_values": [
    {"type_ref": "route-label", "value": "APPROVE"},
    {"type_ref": "route-label", "value": "REJECT"}
  ]
}
```

A choice has exactly one source step, one label type and a finite list of allowed typed values. The step's completion carrier identifies the label field. Its `LABEL` relationships provide the complete label map. Every allowed value appears exactly once, and every label edge targets one step. An ordinary `SEQUENCE` edge cannot coexist with label edges on the same choice step. A declared `FAILURE` relationship is separate from the success label map.

The label is read from `route_label_field` in the exact native record of a matching terminal `EFFECT_OBSERVED` event. The proposal cannot carry a route label. A dispatch observation cannot carry one. The lifecycle does not use a default label, a language model, a connector status or a process-local value. If the terminal effect's label is absent, unknown, duplicated, or fails the declared type, the effect record is retained and the lifecycle admits `STOPPED` with `LABEL_INVALID`. No successor is active.

The static definition is inadmissible when a route is missing, duplicated, ambiguously typed, or points outside the definition. A schema-admitted choice whose label domain lacks one exact target is `DEFINITION_INVALID`. A reference to an undeclared target is `REFERENCE_INVALID`. A static mapping error is an input refusal at validation or deployment. It is separate from an invalid label observed at runtime.

Every completion, routing, expiry and obligation-discharge rule below applies only after `LIFECYCLE.md` classifies the occurrence and event as eligible to progress. A `BLOCKED_DISPUTE`, closed, late, unknown, unexpected, foreign, conflicting or budget-disputed case retains evidence and reconciles exposure under the lifecycle rule without applying a normal composition route, except where that rule states a specific evidence-only state change.

requirements.title: Restricted canonical JSON
requirements.observable_behavior:
Policy artifact bytes are UTF-8 JSON without a byte-order mark, duplicate map keys, invalid UTF-8, lone surrogate code points, JSON number tokens or nonfinite values. JSON null, Booleans, strings, lists and maps are permitted. Numerical quantities and counts are strings in the grammars below. Decode duplicate keys before map construction; a parser that silently keeps one value is not conforming. Unicode normalization is forbidden.

Canonical serialization is the number-free RFC 8785 subset, defined completely here: no whitespace; map keys ordered by their UTF-16 code-unit sequence; lists preserve order; quote and backslash escaped; U+0008, U+0009, U+000A, U+000C and U+000D escaped as `\b`, `\t`, `\n`, `\f` and `\r`; other U+0000 through U+001F characters use lowercase `\u00xx`; remaining scalar values appear directly as UTF-8. Slash is not escaped. Null and Boolean tokens are lowercase. Canonical set order compares complete canonical member UTF-8 bytes and forbids duplicates. Identifier sets use raw UTF-8 byte order.

Fields ending `_bytes_base64` use the standard Base64 alphabet, canonical padding and no whitespace. Reencoding decoded bytes must reproduce the string. Admission compares received artifact bytes to their canonical serialization. The incoming transport request envelope need not be canonical; protocol responses are canonical under `PROTOCOL.md`. Neither transport nor the runner may normalize artifact bytes before their admission boundary.

requirements.title: Digests and versions
requirements.observable_behavior:
For a role token `kind`, `digest(kind,value)` is `sha256:` followed by lowercase SHA-256 of the UTF-8 prefix `seampoint.work-class/1.0.0-draft.2/`, then `kind`, then one line-feed byte, then canonical UTF-8 value bytes. The prefix is versioned. Subsystem documents name role tokens and exact digest subjects. A digest establishes content identity, not authentication, authorship or organizational authority.

`specification_pin` is `sha256:` plus the raw SHA-256 of this candidate's exact manifest bytes. A pin supplied by an input must equal the consumer's selected manifest. Artifact and schema versions cannot be selected by ambient file discovery. Every changed frozen normative document, schema or expected result receives a new candidate identity; previous qualification remains bound to its previous identity. Development files are not frozen until a manifest exists and a freeze record identifies them.

The lifecycle and review digest kinds are `work-class-definition`, `deployment-authorization-subject`, `deployment-authorization`, `deployment-activation`, `relationship`, `occurrence`, `runtime-event`, `proposal`, `native-request`, `dispatch-native-request`, `dispatch-attempt`, `connector-binding`, `executor-binding`, `permit`, `dispatch`, `native-evidence`, `native-evidence-fact`, `no-effect-completion`, `deadline-activation`, `lifecycle-reservation-event`, `outcome`, `obligation`, `work-state-core`, `work-state`, `decision-receipt`, `lifecycle-transaction`, `boundary`, `correspondence-subject`, `correspondence` and `evidence`. The `deployment-authorization-subject` digest subject is the complete deployment-authorization record with `authorization_evidence_digest` omitted. The organizational-authorization evidence binds that subject digest. The `deployment-authorization` digest subject is the complete deployment-authorization record, including the evidence digest. The complete record can therefore bind the evidence without a cycle. A relationship digest hashes one complete relationship. The occurrence digest subject is exactly `{specification_pin,work_class_digest,instance_id,step_id,ordinal,predecessor_occurrence_ids,enclosing,object_key}`; `occurrence_id` is not part of that subject. A permit, dispatch, outcome or decision receipt contains an identifier computed from the corresponding digest kind over the complete record with that computed identifier omitted. An obligation digest subject is exactly `{kind,construct_id,pass,source_occurrence_ids,branch_id,object_key,join_step_id}`; mutable status and evidence are not part of its identity. `runtime-event` hashes the complete admitted lifecycle event and supplies `event_digest` wherever that value is retained. `proposal` separately hashes the same complete admitted `PROPOSE` event for its proposal role. `native-evidence` hashes the complete lifecycle native-evidence record. `native-evidence-fact` omits only its evidence ID and evidence reference. LIFE-009 defines the dispatch-native-request, dispatch-attempt and connector-binding subjects; LIFE-010 defines the no-effect-completion and lifecycle-reservation-event subjects; and LIFE-014 defines the deadline-activation subject. The proposal form of lifecycle-reservation-event is defined in LIFE-007. `work-state-core` hashes the complete next work state after replacing `receipts` and `replays` with empty arrays. The `work-state` subject is the complete state after omitting `transaction_digest` from every replay record; those values are verified independently. `lifecycle-transaction` hashes exactly `{state_before_digest,event_digest,decision_receipt_digest,state_after_core_digest,budget_results}`. The budget results retain the complete single-registry result where the occurrence uses shared budgets. `boundary` hashes the complete boundary record. `correspondence-subject` hashes the complete correspondence record with its nested `review` omitted; `correspondence` hashes the complete correspondence record; and `evidence` hashes any complete evidence record. LIFE-019 defines the lifecycle construction order and retained replay fields. These projections prevent circular references while retaining exact transition bindings.

References resolve only against complete explicitly supplied records or the mappings in `schema-bundle.json`. A digest-shaped identifier without its required record is not evidence. The same identifier cannot bind different records within one admitted input. A complete successor distribution includes the manifest, all named files, examples, exact suite and implementation dependencies. Installing pinned dependencies is separate from offline operation.

requirements.title: Exact values and time
requirements.observable_behavior:
A natural integer is `0` or a nonzero decimal digit followed by decimal digits. A nonnegative decimal has an integer part in that grammar and optionally a point followed by digits whose last digit is nonzero. There is no sign, exponent, leading zero, trailing fractional zero or binary-floating-point interpretation. Where a signed INTEGER or DECIMAL is expressly supported, a single leading minus is permitted except for negative zero. Compare and add exact base-ten mathematical values. Unit conversion is never implicit.

UTC instants use `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` or that form with exactly nine fractional digits before `Z`, as selected explicitly by the relevant temporal configuration. Years are 0001 through 9999; month/day must exist in the proleptic Gregorian calendar; hours are 00–23 and minutes/seconds 00–59. No leap seconds, offsets or 24:00 are accepted. Exact seconds and nanoseconds determine order. Temporal arithmetic must not use the host's local zone or ambient time. A subsystem that supports a narrower explicit grammar states it in its schema and prose; no string comparison replaces calendar validation.

The aggregate calendar profile pins IANA tzdb `2025a`. Consumers use the same transition data. The host may supply a clock sample only according to the declared source and precision. An unavailable clock is an explicit input, not permission to consult a machine clock.

requirements.title: Admission and resource boundaries
requirements.observable_behavior:
Transport failures are distinct from artifact admission and from policy decisions. A malformed event or invalid supplied state leaves governed state and reservations unchanged. A valid proposal that violates policy can return the declared policy refusal, with the record changes expressly specified by that transition. Unknown policy facts never become default permission.

Unless a subsystem explicitly imposes a different advertised bound, support is bounded to 64 definitions, 256 operations, 1024 members in an ordinary collection, 128 digits in a numerical coefficient, 64 expression levels and 4096 expression nodes. A proposal-capable step may declare at most 64 request fields, 64 prior-effect bindings and 64 prior-actor separations; its completion record may contain those 64 bound fields plus one distinct status field and one distinct route-label field. A work-class `maximum_proposals`, `maximum_activations` or `maximum_actuations` cannot exceed 4096; `maximum_active_obligations` cannot exceed 4096; and `maximum_fanout_objects` cannot exceed 1024. The closed work-class schema permits at most 425869 readback leaf or empty-collection paths, so each correspondence path inventory permits that many members and its residue inventory permits 426893 members, including the 1024 possible source obligations. Active and completed occurrences, proposals, permits, obligations, deadlines and fan-out passes have the explicit bounds in their schemas. Dispatch, outcome, clock, receipt and replay histories remain append-only so the consumer can admit evidence for existing work after new proposals stop. Input-size transport controls are reported separately and do not excuse a crash on an otherwise supported input. Resource exhaustion, timeout and implementation exceptions are execution failures, never governance results. Implementations must reject supported-shape inputs above a stated contract limit using the specified refusal or retained limit decision before evaluating or extending governed work.

requirements.title: Reviewable meaning
requirements.observable_behavior:
Readback renders every operative policy field with its complete canonical value. It covers nested scalar leaves and empty collections; object/list containers with descendants are represented by their descendants. Each line's `path` is one complete JSON Pointer. The pointer root is the empty string, tokens escape `~` as `~0` and `/` as `~1`, and array indices use natural-integer spelling. Lines sort by the raw UTF-8 bytes of the complete escaped pointer string, without interpreting array indices numerically or unescaping tokens for comparison. Each `value` is the WCS2-001 canonical JSON serialization of that scalar or empty collection, carried as a JSON string in the readback line. The deterministic machine rendering is not a claim to have produced or understood a faithful English paraphrase.

Correspondence accounts in both directions for declared source obligations and operative work-class provisions. The provision universe is the complete JSON-pointer leaf and empty-collection path set produced by deterministic readback of the exact work-class definition, excluding no field. A correspondence mapping binds one declared source obligation to one or more paths. The mapping source-obligation IDs plus `uncovered_source_obligation_ids` form an exact disjoint partition of the complete source-obligation inventory. The union of every mapping's paths plus `unsupported_provision_paths` covers the complete readback path set; no unsupported path may also be mapped. One provision path may support several source obligations, but each `(source_obligation_id,provision_path)` edge appears only once. Every uncovered obligation and unsupported path has exactly one residue row with its kind, exact subject, disposition and nonempty explanation. There is at most one mapping for each source obligation. The mappings sort by source obligation ID; their path sets, uncovered IDs and unsupported paths sort by raw UTF-8 order and contain no duplicates. Residue records sort first by `kind` and then by `subject`, both in raw UTF-8 order, and contain no duplicate pair.

The correspondence record binds the exact work-class digest and the work class's source ID and revision. Its nested accepted review has subject digest `digest("correspondence-subject", correspondence_without_review)`. A valid correspondence record and review have accepted status, the selected candidate pin and exact subject bindings. Pending, rejected or deferred records cannot satisfy acceptance. This mechanical check proves inventory partitioning and exact record binding. It does not prove that the English obligation was understood, that a mapped provision is faithful, or that a residue disposition is acceptable. Source confirmation, policy decisions and organizational authorization remain separate review acts. Deployment under LIFE-003 requires each of them, as distinct accepted records, together with an accepted correspondence record for the exact definition. Changed subjects require new evidence unless an explicit rule permits continued reliance.

Generic readback covers every admitted aggregate, authority and work-class definition, boundary record and evidence record. Runtime and review roles use the same exact bytes and candidate pin as the evaluator roles. The historical candidates remain available under their own identities and do not certify this candidate.

requirements.title: Host responsibilities
requirements.observable_behavior:
Hosts establish the real identities of people and machines, the authenticity and organizational basis of supplied records, truthful observation providers, exact projection of native invocation arguments, protected history, serialized event submission and durable commitment of returned state. A consumer checks the supplied declarations and bindings mechanically. Consistent false records can pass mechanical checks; the contract does not authenticate them through hashing.

Every evidence record that an operation relies on for a human act has an attributable return. The host retains at least the complete canonical bytes of the act as returned, their digest, the actor identifier asserted by the identity provider named in the applicable boundary record, the return channel's provider and source, the host instant of return, and those return bytes under the record's evidence reference. The record's `provenance_digest` identifies that retained return; the consumer checks its format but cannot recompute it. A detached signature over the canonical act bytes by a key that the identity provider binds to the actor satisfies the authenticity obligation. The conformance suite has no key material and cannot verify signatures, so signature format and verification remain host obligations outside this contract. The reservation administration return in RESERVATION-RECORDS is one instance of this rule.

Permission applies to the exact operation, occurrence, authority, observation revision and state evaluated. Every proposal-capable step declares a positive finite `permit_seconds` value. A successful proposal fixes the current authority and observation snapshot until the resulting permit's exclusive expiry, which may be earlier when a shared-budget policy requires it. The organization's authorization of the exact definition and candidate accepts this snapshot rule. The host commits the complete transition atomically before native dispatch and dispatches only the exact permitted request before expiry. After expiry it must obtain a new proposal and current evaluation. Every covered mutation path passes through this enforcement boundary. A reference in-memory lock does not demonstrate durable crash recovery or distributed atomicity.

Dispatch, acknowledgement and native effect are distinct facts. A timeout is not proof that an effect did not occur. Hosts retain unknown outcomes, use supported native deduplication where available, and do not redispatch blindly. Late attributable evidence may establish a past reserved effect even after scheduling stops, without granting permission for new work. Conflicting effects remain recorded and disputed. No rollback, cancellation or compensation is implied.

## Profile documents and evidence

`AUTHORITY.md` defines direct business-authority application. `AGGREGATES.md` defines bounded aggregate evaluation. `RESERVATIONS.md` defines shared exposure and the reference host boundary. `LIFECYCLE.md` defines proposal, permit, dispatch, effect and atomic work-and-budget transitions. `COMPOSITION.md` defines choice and bounded loops, deadlines, structured parallel work and frozen fan-out. `EXTERNAL-DEPENDENCIES.md` records host obligations. `PROTOCOL.md` defines the adapter and qualification report. Schemas and worked examples accompany the corresponding documents.

Requirements and cases must identify whether they are mechanical, documentary or human assessments. Every claimed mechanical requirement needs a decisive case that reaches it. Cases, mutations, independent implementation questions, failures and reports are retained under the matching conformance candidate. Internal reviews are evidence of internal review, not reputable external endorsement.

requirements.title: Transport and schema resolution
requirements.observable_behavior:
A program reads one restricted UTF-8 JSON object per line from standard input and returns one canonical JSON object followed by one LF byte on standard output. A request has exactly `protocol`, `request_id`, `operation`, and object-valued `input`. A normal response has exactly the same `protocol`, `request_id` and operation plus a closed `result`. `protocol.schema.json` has a top-level union of those closed request and response envelopes. Every protocol-error response uses the adapter's supported protocol identity, including when the input named another value. If a parsed object has a recognized operation but the protocol or envelope is invalid, the response uses that recognized operation and result `{"status":"REFUSED","code":"PROTOCOL_INVALID","path":""}`. If the operation is an unrecognized but valid identifier, the protocol-error response echoes it. A missing or malformed operation becomes null. A valid request identifier is echoed; a missing or malformed identifier becomes null. Invalid UTF-8, duplicate keys, JSON numbers, invalid Unicode and an unterminated final line are transport errors. The program terminates nonzero without a governance result for that line. Diagnostics use standard error. Processing one request cannot depend on a fixture identifier, corpus file or process-local request history.

The recognized operations are `capabilities`, `validate`, `evaluate`, `aggregate-step`, `deploy`, `step`, `readback`, and `check-evidence`. A consumer claims the operations and roles it implements in `capabilities`. A profile or role outside that claim returns `ROLE_UNSUPPORTED`. A missing or unknown required kind returns `SCHEMA_INVALID`. The consumer cannot fall back to another protocol.

The candidate supplies a closed schema graph. `schema-bundle.json` maps each exact schema URI to one candidate-relative file. A consumer resolves a listed URI only through that mapping. An unlisted URI is unresolved and returns `REFERENCE_INVALID` for an otherwise admitted artifact reference. A source reference, artifact identifier or schema reference cannot trigger network or undeclared filesystem access. `aggregate.schema.json`, `authority.schema.json`, `reservation.schema.json`, `work-class.schema.json`, `lifecycle.schema.json`, `evidence.schema.json`, `boundary.schema.json`, and `protocol.schema.json` are the complete public graph.

Every public object boundary is closed. Each schema object either declares its complete properties and rejects additional properties, or selects a finite set of closed variants. A schema-control failure blocks candidate freeze when any public object relies on an unconstrained `type: object`.

requirements.title: Capabilities and roles
requirements.observable_behavior:
`capabilities` input is exactly `{}`. Its result has exactly `status`, `protocol`, `specification_pin`, `roles`, `operations`, `tzdb`, and `limits`. `status` is `CAPABILITIES`; `protocol` identifies this adapter; and the pin is the SHA-256 digest of the exact draft-2 contract manifest bytes. Roles and operations are sorted, unique UTF-8 identifier lists. `tzdb` is `2025a` when calendar aggregate evaluation is supported and null otherwise. A capabilities result is a claim to test, not a certificate.

Runtime roles are `LINEAR_WORK_RUNTIME`, `CHOICE_LOOP_RUNTIME`, `DEADLINE_RUNTIME`, and `PARALLEL_FANOUT_RUNTIME`. Their profiles are cumulative in the order defined by `LIFECYCLE.md`. The exact pairs are `LINEAR` with `LINEAR_WORK_RUNTIME`, `CHOICE_LOOPS` with `CHOICE_LOOP_RUNTIME`, `DEADLINES` with `DEADLINE_RUNTIME`, and `PARALLEL_FANOUT` with `PARALLEL_FANOUT_RUNTIME`. Any other admitted-enum pair is `ROLE_UNSUPPORTED` before definition or state checks. The remaining roles are `AGGREGATE_EVALUATOR`, `AUTHORITY_EVALUATOR`, `SHARED_BUDGET_TRANSITIONS`, `REFERENCE_SINGLE_PROCESS_CONTENTION`, and `REVIEW_EVIDENCE`. A claimed runtime role includes the authority and shared-budget consequences of every admitted operation. An implementation cannot claim that its caller performed those parts outside the tested lifecycle.

A pure transition consumer cannot claim `REFERENCE_SINGLE_PROCESS_CONTENTION`. That role requires separate tests of serialized access to one work state and every affected shared budget, atomic commit, two-client contention, and export for restart. It does not imply durable storage or distributed coordination.

requirements.title: Operation contracts
requirements.observable_behavior:
`protocol.schema.json` selects the exact closed input and result schema for each operation. Duplicate keys and malformed JSON are transport failures before artifact admission. Within a decoded artifact, a duplicate key returns `ARTIFACT_ENCODING_INVALID`; a forbidden JSON-number token or a canonical-byte mismatch returns `ARTIFACT_NONCANONICAL`. Other structural errors in an operation input return `SCHEMA_INVALID`. Once a request's state is structurally admitted, a stateful refusal returns that exact supplied state and every supplied budget state unchanged. A malformed outer request has no admitted state to echo.

### `validate` and `readback`

Both inputs have exactly `kind`, `specification_pin`, and `artifact_bytes_base64`. The recognized artifact kinds are `AGGREGATE_DEFINITION`, `AUTHORITY_DEFINITION`, `WORK_CLASS`, `BOUNDARY_RECORD`, and `EVIDENCE_RECORD`. Base64 carries the original artifact bytes through the adapter envelope. The consumer decodes the bytes, enforces the restricted canonical JSON rules, checks the selected candidate and schema identity, resolves references only through the schema bundle and then applies the subsystem's static checks. Successful artifact digests use `aggregate-definition`, the authority definition's declared domain, `work-class-definition`, `boundary`, or `evidence` respectively.

Validation success is exactly `{"status":"ACCEPTED","digest":<artifact digest>}`. Readback success contains exactly `status`, `digest`, and `lines`; `status` is `READBACK`. Each line contains exactly a JSON Pointer `path` and canonical scalar or empty-collection `value` string. Readback covers every operative field. It does not interpret source prose or prove fidelity to an English policy.

### `evaluate`

The input has exactly `kind` and `request`. `AGGREGATE` selects the complete aggregate input and result. `AUTHORITY` selects the complete authority input and result. Both receive explicit clock and evidence facts. An authority result of `READY_FOR_RESERVATION` identifies an exact current proposal that has passed the authority checks. It is not a permit and cannot authorize dispatch.

### `aggregate-step`

The input is the complete reservation transition input in `reservation.schema.json`, without another kind wrapper. `REGISTER`, `RESERVE`, `RENEW`, `SETTLE`, and `RELEASE` are reservation event kinds rather than adapter operations. A transition result includes the complete receipt, receipt digest, next reservation state, state digest, and replay flag. A stateful refusal echoes the exact prior reservation state. The independent interface and the composite lifecycle use the same reservation semantics.

### `deploy`

The input is the closed `deployInput` in `lifecycle.schema.json`. It contains exactly the selected profile and corresponding role, candidate pin, complete work-class definition and digest. The selected profile equals `definition.profile`; an admitted profile-role pair with another definition profile is `BINDING_MISMATCH`. It also contains instance identity, complete deployment authorization, the complete organizational-authorization, correspondence, source-confirmation and policy-decision evidence records named by it, an available authorization clock and the exact `initial_clocks` array required by root deadlines. The authorization binds the exact candidate pin, work-class digest, profile, role and instance, along with the organization and the four evidence digests. LIFE-003 defines the checks on the three review records. The organizational evidence binds the `deployment-authorization-subject` digest of the record before its evidence-digest field is populated; the complete record receives a separate `deployment-authorization` digest. The implementation verifies both digests and the evidence status, subject, organization and validity at the authorization-clock instant. A null deployment-authorization expiry has no fixed upper bound; a nonnull expiry is exclusive and must be later than that clock. A bare accepted status and ambient time are not sufficient. `initial_clocks` follows LIFE-003 and is empty when no root deadline requires it.

Success is the closed `deployResult`. It identifies the profile, role, instance, work-class digest and complete deployment-authorization digest and returns the complete initial work state and digest. That state retains the deployment-authorization record, the four evidence records, their exact subject, record and evidence digests, and the authorization clock so a restart can recompute every binding and time relation. It activates the root occurrence. It creates no operation permit, shared reservation, dispatch or effect record. A malformed request that prevents profile and role admission returns the generic shape refusal. Once those values are admitted, a deployment failure returns the closed lifecycle refusal `{status,profile,role,code,path}` with the exact admitted profile and role and no state.

### `step`

The input is the closed `stepInput` in `lifecycle.schema.json`. It contains exactly the selected profile and role, candidate pin, complete work-class definition and digest, complete prior state and digest, and one closed lifecycle event. The selected profile equals `definition.profile`; the state profile and role equal the request pair; and the state work-class digest equals the supplied definition digest. An otherwise admitted mismatch is `BINDING_MISMATCH`. The event is exactly one of `PROPOSE`, `DISPATCH_OBSERVED`, `EFFECT_OBSERVED`, or `CLOCK`.

`PROPOSE` contains one exact occurrence, native request, executor, credential set, complete authority input, zero or one required registry-scoped budget input with expected revision, accepted clock revision and observation digests. It represents either the first proposal for an active occurrence or the renewal of an expired, undispatched permit under LIFE-007. A nonempty input names one reservation registry and the sorted anchor set changed by its one complete reservation transition. The consumer first checks declared bindings to unique completed ancestor effects, evaluates current authority, checks declared cross-occurrence actor separation and then applies the reservation rules. Success returns one permit containing the exact retained bases and changes the work state and the one affected reservation-registry state together. An authority or separation withholding records `WITHHELD` and leaves the registry unchanged. A reservation policy withholding records both the work decision and the registry's withholding receipt and next revision. A malformed, stale or wrongly bound proposal is an admission refusal and leaves every supplied state unchanged.

`DISPATCH_OBSERVED` contains the complete committed permit, exact native request, connector identity, attempt, acknowledgement and the exact latest retained available clock revision used to validate the attempt timeline. The attempt time cannot precede the permit clock or follow the selected dispatch clock, and permit expiry is tested against that attempt time. A changed native request with `NOT_SENT` and no accepted acknowledgement produces `DISPATCH_REFUSED`; any mismatch that may have reached the connector produces `DISPUTED` and an unknown occurrence state. A matching attempt is retained. Its acknowledgement does not settle exposure or advance the work graph.

`EFFECT_OBSERVED` has a governed branch and a foreign branch. The governed branch contains the complete permit, dispatch digest, provider-native operation identity, native evidence, actual scalar fields, typed collection fields, effect status, event time, observation time, nullable completion authorization, zero or one registry input, and the activation-clock copies required by newly activated deadlines. The foreign branch supplies null permit, dispatch and completion authorization plus the provider-native operation identity. An authority-only foreign effect supplies an empty affected-anchor set and no registry input. A budget-bearing foreign effect supplies a nonempty exact affected-anchor set and one matching registry input. An exact governed effect can settle reservations and advance the graph. The effect, dispatch-attempt, observation and selected registry-clock times must satisfy LIFE-010; a well-formed established effect with a contradictory claimed timeline is retained and disputed rather than allowed to route or free capacity. Unknown, foreign, unexpected, conflicting and late effects are retained according to `LIFECYCLE.md` and `RESERVATION-RECORDS.md`. No effect can complete an occurrence without a committed permit and exact dispatch binding.

`CLOCK` contains one exact available, unavailable or conflicting clock record and the activation-clock copies required by any successor deadlines created by expiry routing. Only an available admitted clock revision advances runtime time and evaluates deadline predicates. Proposal, dispatch and effect timestamps do not advance the lifecycle clock.

Success is the closed `stepResult`. It contains exactly `status`, `profile`, `role`, `decision`, `decision_digest`, `permit`, `budget_results`, `state`, `state_digest`, `transition_state_digest`, `transaction_digest`, and `replay`. Each affected budget result contains its reservation-registry digest, affected anchor set and complete reservation transition result. `transition_state_digest` is the original decision's `state_after_core_digest`; `state_digest` identifies the complete returned state through the projection in LIFE-019. They are different identities. On exact replay, the decision, permit, budget results, transition-state digest and transaction digest are the original transition values, while `state` and `state_digest` are current. The transaction digest binds the prior work state, event, decision, original next-state core and every original budget result without creating a circular digest. The host commits the complete transition before dispatch.

An exact replay returns the retained historical transition fields and the current complete state with `replay:true` and creates no new state revision. Reuse of an event identifier with changed canonical bytes returns `REPLAY_CONFLICT`. A new event submitted against a stale state or budget revision returns the corresponding revision refusal.

The reference host reports authoritative initial-root installation through the closed `hostDeploymentResult` and commit-before-dispatch through the closed `hostCommitResult` in `lifecycle.schema.json`. These host results are exercised by the reference-host harness and are not adapter operations. An exact duplicate installation returns the established state as an idempotent replay; a conflicting installation returns `INSTANCE_OCCUPIED`. `COMMIT_FAILED` returns the unchanged authoritative work and budget digests and `dispatch_performed:false`.

### `check-evidence`

The input is one of two closed evidence inputs in `evidence.schema.json`. The basic form contains the profile, `REVIEW_EVIDENCE` role, candidate pin, exact subject and a source-confirmation, policy-decision, organizational-authorization or review record. `subject.subject_digest` is the externally computed digest of the exact artifact or record named by `subject.kind` and `subject_id`; it is not a digest of the subject wrapper. The evidence record's subject digest must equal it. The consumer checks candidate, pin, exact equality and accepted status. Variant-specific scope arrays are closed, sorted record content, but this basic input supplies no expected scope universe and therefore does not establish scope sufficiency.

The correspondence form also supplies the complete work-class definition and digest plus one correspondence record. The subject kind is `WORK_CLASS`; its ID equals the definition ID; and `correspondence.subject_digest`, `subject.subject_digest`, `correspondence.work_class_digest`, and `work_class_digest` all equal `digest("work-class-definition",work_class)`. The input pin and subject pin both equal `work_class.specification_pin`, and the input profile equals `work_class.profile`. The record source ID and revision equal the definition's source. The consumer derives the complete source-obligation inventory and the complete readback provision-path universe, verifies the exact source-obligation partition, the complete provision-path coverage with no mapped/unsupported overlap, edge uniqueness, and one residue row per uncovered member, and verifies the nested accepted review against `digest("correspondence-subject",correspondence_without_review)`. A digest, identity, pin, partition, residue, or review-subject mismatch is `BINDING_MISMATCH`. A structurally missing review is `SCHEMA_INVALID`; a present review whose status is not `ACCEPTED` is `EVIDENCE_NOT_ACCEPTED`. This establishes mechanical coverage accounting and exact review binding, not semantic fidelity.

A successful result contains exactly `status`, `profile`, `role`, `subject_digest`, `evidence_digest`, and `specification_pin`. `evidence_digest` is `digest("evidence",evidence)`. A failed check whose profile and role were admitted returns those identities in the closed `EVIDENCE_INVALID` result with `BINDING_MISMATCH`, `EVIDENCE_NOT_ACCEPTED`, `EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE` or `SCHEMA_INVALID`. A malformed input uses the generic shape refusal. The operation establishes only the mechanical facts stated for its basic or correspondence form. It does not authenticate the actor, prove observation truth, establish the semantic adequacy of a scope or mapping, or qualify a production deployment. Deployment separately checks the full deployment-authorization record, its organizational-authorization evidence and its correspondence, source-confirmation and policy-decision evidence under LIFE-003.

requirements.title: Evaluation order and result classes
requirements.observable_behavior:
The adapter applies checks in this order: transport and envelope; protocol, operation, candidate, role and profile selection; closed schema; canonical bytes and declared artifact identity where applicable; definition and state digest; exact replay; instance, occurrence, proposal, permit, dispatch, evidence and clock binding; event prerequisites; the retained proposal-count ceiling for `PROPOSE`; current authority, including its required clock and observations; the initial-proposal actuation ceiling; shared-budget revision and policy; effect-carrier classification and declared route selection; effect- or clock-driven structural composition preflight. A higher-precedence failure determines the result. Permit renewal does not use the actuation ceiling.

An admission refusal has `status:REFUSED`, a typed code and `path:""` in this candidate. The empty path avoids implementation-dependent diagnostic pointers; implementations may report diagnostics outside the canonical conformance result. A refusal creates no governed decision. Where the runtime state has been admitted, the lifecycle refusal also carries the selected profile and role and the exact supplied work and budget states. An admitted policy decision records the event identity and digest in the state checkpoint, requires the host to retain the complete canonical request and response preimages under LIFE-019, and advances the work-state revision even when its disposition is negative or stopping. `WITHHELD`, `DISPATCH_REFUSED`, `OUTCOME_RETAINED`, `FAILED`, `EXPIRED`, `STOPPED`, and `DISPUTED` are admitted decisions rather than input refusals.

The common and lifecycle admission-refusal vocabulary is `ADMINISTRATION_NOT_ESTABLISHED`, `ARTIFACT_ENCODING_INVALID`, `ARTIFACT_NONCANONICAL`, `BINDING_MISMATCH`, `CLOCK_INVALID`, `DEFINITION_CONFLICT`, `DEFINITION_INVALID`, `DEPENDENCY_MISMATCH`, `DIGEST_MISMATCH`, `EVIDENCE_UNAVAILABLE`, `INPUT_INVALID`, `INSTANCE_NOT_ACTIVE`, `LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `OCCURRENCE_CONFLICT`, `OCCURRENCE_NOT_ACTIVE`, `PREREQUISITE_MISSING`, `PROTOCOL_INVALID`, `REFERENCE_INVALID`, `REPLAY_CONFLICT`, `RESERVATION_NOT_FOUND`, `REVISION_CONFLICT`, `ROLE_UNSUPPORTED`, `SCHEMA_INVALID`, `STATE_INVALID`, `TYPE_INVALID`, `UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE`, `UNSUPPORTED_RELATION` and `VERSION_UNSUPPORTED`. Embedded authority and reservation admission failures retain the same code from this union. Direct authority evaluation also has the closed policy-refusal codes `ACT_CONFLICT`, `GATE_REQUIRED`, `ACT_NOT_AUTHORIZED`, `ACT_NOT_ACCEPTED`, and `AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED` defined by `AUTHORITY-CHECKS.md` and `authority.schema.json`; the lifecycle maps those results to admitted `WITHHELD` decisions rather than admission refusals. Decision reason codes are a separate vocabulary defined by the applicable lifecycle or subsystem rule.

Expected results are derived from the normative rule and exact input before either implementation output is disclosed. An implementation result may reveal an error in the text or expectation. It cannot establish a replacement answer. A correction to normative text, schema or expected bytes after freeze creates a new candidate identity.

requirements.title: Suite, runner and reports
requirements.observable_behavior:
Every case has exactly `id`, `operation`, `input`, `expected`, `requirements`, and `derivation`. The expected value is the complete output, including state, permit, budget results, receipts and digests where applicable. Case and path identities are unique. The suite manifest binds the candidate and pin, mandatory roles and requirements, exact case and review hashes, coverage inventory and frozen mutation catalog.

The runner compares canonical result bytes and contains no policy evaluator. Every mandatory case runs. A missing case, skip, duplicate result, malformed response, crash, timeout or output overflow fails qualification. Execution failure cannot count as a governance refusal or successful mutation detection.

The runner executes locally selected trusted programs in a minimal environment with bounded output, a default 30-second request timeout, an 8 MiB limit for each output stream and process-group cleanup. These controls are not a hostile-code sandbox. Installation may obtain pinned public dependencies. Scored execution uses no network, model, real service credential or adjacent repository.

Reports identify exact contract, suite, implementation and dependency hashes, claimed roles and profiles, runtime versions, every case and failure, mutation results, generated-input and state-interchange controls, reproduction commands and unsupported roles. Reports distinguish semantic consumer qualification, the reference host's serialized single-process qualification, documented host obligations and deployment assurance.

requirements.title: Cross-profile limits and authority
requirements.observable_behavior:
Every concrete operation, branch, object, loop occurrence and deadline target is subject to the authority requirements and aggregate or shared budget rules declared by the work class. A grant covering an object type does not prove authority for an object value outside its scope. A grant used for one operation occurrence does not silently authorize a later occurrence. The authority evaluator's complete result is rechecked for each proposal and occurrence.

A structured split, join, or fan-out transition cannot bypass reservations. If the definition requires shared budgets for branch or object operations, the `PROPOSE` event for each operation uses the current budget states and exact revision. The split or expansion transition records obligations and active occurrences; it does not grant permits for every child. Each child requires a separate proposal and atomic authority/reservation decision.

A stop leaves all committed effects, actuation records, reservation exposure, unknown outcomes and evidence in the state. The profile does not treat stop as cancellation or no effect. The reservation contract determines whether later settlement, dispute or authorized release is possible.
